title.zh: 卷四百四十七 列傳第二百〇六 忠義二 霍安國 李涓 李邈劉翊 徐揆 陳遘 趙不試 趙令峸 唐重郭忠孝 程迪 徐徽言 向子韶 楊邦乂
title.en: Volume 447 Biographies 206: Loyalty and Righteousness 2: Huo Anguo, Li Juan, Li Miaoliuyi, Xu Kui, Chen Gou, Zhao Bushi, Zhao Lingcheng, Tang Zhongguozhongxiao, Cheng Di, Xu Huiyan, Xiang Zishao, Yang Bangyi
title.raw: 卷四百四十七 列傳第二百〇六 忠義二 霍安國 李涓 李邈劉翊 徐揆 陳遘 趙不試 趙令峸 唐重郭忠孝 程迪 徐徽言 向子韶 楊邦乂 Volume 447 Biographies 206: Loyalty and Righteousness 2: Huo Anguo, Li Juan, Li Miaoliuyi, Xu Kui, Chen Gou, Zhao Bushi, Zhao Lingcheng, Tang Zhongguozhongxiao, Cheng Di, Xu Huiyan, Xiang Zishao, Yang Bangyi

sentences.zh: 霍安國 李涓 李邈 劉翊 徐揆 陳遘 趙不試 趙令峸 唐重 郭忠孝 程迪 徐徽言 向子韶 楊邦乂

translations.literal: Huo Anguo, Li Juan, Li Miao, Liu Yi, Xu Kui, Chen Gou, Zhao Bushi, Zhao Lingcheng, Tang Chong, Guo Zhongxiao, Cheng Di, Xu Huiyan, Xiang Zishao, Yang Bangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Anguo, Li Juan, Li Miao, Liu Yi, Xu Kui, Chen Gou, Zhao Bushi, Zhao Lingcheng, Tang Chong, Guo Zhongxiao, Cheng Di, Xu Huiyan, Xiang Zishao, and Yang Bangyi.

sentences.zh: 霍安國

translations.literal: Huo Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Anguo.

sentences.zh: 李涓，字浩然，駙馬都尉遵勖曾孫也。

translations.literal: Li Juan, style name Haoran, was the great-grandson of the Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household, Zunxu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Juan, styled Haoran, was a great-grandson of Zunxu, Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.

sentences.zh: 以蔭爲殿直，召試中書，易文階，至通直郎，知鄂州崇陽縣。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he became a Palace Attendant; summoned to the Secretariat for examination, he exchanged to a civil rank, reaching Gentleman for Unimpeded Communication, and served as magistrate of Chongyang County in E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through yin privilege he entered service as a palace attendant; after passing a Secretariat examination he transferred to the civil register, rose to Gentleman for Unimpeded Communication, and was appointed magistrate of Chongyang County in Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，京城被圍，羽檄召天下兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, the capital was besieged; urgent dispatches summoned troops from throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jingkang reign, when the capital was besieged, urgent orders went out summoning troops from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 鄂部縣七，當發二千九百人，皆未集，涓獨以所募六百銳然請行。

translations.literal: E circuit had seven counties that should have raised twenty-nine hundred men; none had yet assembled, but Juan alone, with six hundred he had recruited, boldly asked to march.
translations.idiomatic: Seven counties in the Ezhou circuit were to furnish twenty-nine hundred men, yet none had mustered; Juan alone, with six hundred troops he had raised, volunteered to march at once.

sentences.zh: 或謂：「盍徐之，以須他邑。」

translations.literal: Some said: "Why not wait, to await the other districts?"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him: "Why not wait until the other counties are ready?"

sentences.zh: 涓曰：「事急矣，當持一信報天子，爲東南倡。」

translations.literal: Juan said: "The matter is urgent; one should carry a token of faith to report to the Son of Heaven and be a leader for the southeast."
translations.idiomatic: Juan replied: "Matters are desperate. Someone must carry proof of loyalty to the emperor and rally the southeast."

sentences.zh: 而募士多市人，不能軍，涓出家錢買牛酒激犒之。

translations.literal: Yet most of the recruits were townspeople and could not soldier; Juan spent his own money on cattle and wine to rouse and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his recruits were townsfolk untrained for war; Juan spent his own funds on beef and wine to hearten and reward them.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「吾固知無益，然世受國恩，唯直死耳。

translations.literal: He ordered: "I know well this is of little use, yet our house has received the state's grace for generations; nothing remains but to die upright.
translations.idiomatic: He told them: "I know this may avail little, but our family has enjoyed the state's favor for generations; the only honorable course is to die standing.

sentences.zh: 若曹知法乎，'失將者死'，鈞之一死，死國留名，男兒不朽事也。」

translations.literal: Do you fellows know the law? 'He who loses his general dies'; one death weighed in the balance—dying for the state and leaving a name is an immortal deed for a man."
translations.idiomatic: Do you know the law? 'He who loses his commander must die.' A single death in the scales—to die for the realm and leave one's name is the immortal deed of a true man."

sentences.zh: 衆皆泣。

translations.literal: The crowd all wept.
translations.idiomatic: The men all wept.

sentences.zh: 即日，引而東，北過淮，蒲圻、嘉魚二縣之兵始至，合而前。

translations.literal: That very day he led them east; north of the Huai, troops from Puxian and Jiayu counties at last arrived, and they advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he led them eastward; north of the Huai, the contingents from Puxian and Jiayu finally arrived, and they marched on together.

sentences.zh: 至蔡，天大雪，蔡人忽噪而奔，曰：「敵至矣。」

translations.literal: Reaching Cai, heaven sent great snow; the people of Cai suddenly clamored and fled, crying: "The enemy has come!"
translations.idiomatic: At Cai a heavy snow fell; the townspeople suddenly panicked and fled, shouting that the enemy was upon them.

sentences.zh: 即結陣以待。

translations.literal: He immediately formed ranks to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Juan immediately formed battle lines to meet them.

sentences.zh: 少焉，遊騎果集。

translations.literal: Before long, scouting horsemen indeed gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon enemy scouts appeared in force.

sentences.zh: 涓馳馬先犯其鋒，下皆步卒，蒙鹵盾徑進，頗殺其騎，且走。

translations.literal: Juan spurred his horse first to strike their vanguard; below were all foot soldiers, who advanced straight on with covered shields, killing quite a few of their horsemen, and the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Juan charged first at the enemy van; his foot soldiers advanced under covered shields, killed many horsemen, and drove the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 涓乘勝追北十餘里，大與敵遇，飛矢蝟集，二縣兵亟舍去。

translations.literal: Juan pursued the fleeing foe northward for more than ten li, then met the enemy in strength; arrows flew thick as hedgehogs, and the two counties' troops quickly abandoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the pursuit northward for more than ten li, he met the main enemy force; arrows fell thick as quills, and the troops from the two counties fled at once.

sentences.zh: 涓創甚，猶血戰，大呼叱左右負己，遂死焉，年五十三。

translations.literal: Juan was badly wounded yet still fought in blood, shouting for those at his side to carry him, and there he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Badly wounded, he fought on in a welter of blood, ordering his men to carry him forward, and died on the field at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 士卒死者六七。

translations.literal: Six or seven tenths of the soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Six or seven out of ten of his soldiers perished.

sentences.zh: 上官有忌涓者，脅亡卒誣已遁。

translations.literal: A superior who bore Juan a grudge coerced a surviving soldier to accuse him of having fled.
translations.idiomatic: A superior who envied Juan forced a survivor to claim he had fled.

sentences.zh: 明年，金兵去，蔡人以其屍歸。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Jin army withdrew, the people of Cai returned his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after the Jin withdrew, the people of Cai brought back his body.

sentences.zh: 朝廷錄其忠，贈朝奉郎，官其三子。

translations.literal: The court recorded his loyalty, posthumously enfeoffing him as Gentleman for Court Audience and appointing his three sons to office.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored his loyalty, posthumously promoting him to Gentleman for Court Audience and granting office to his three sons.

sentences.zh: 李邈，字彥思，臨江軍清江人。

translations.literal: Li Miao, style name Yansi, was a native of Qingjiang in Linjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Miao, styled Yansi, came from Qingjiang in Linjiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 唐宗室宰相適之之後。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of the Tang imperial clansman and chancellor Li Shizhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from Li Shizhi, a Tang imperial clansman who served as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 少有才略，精悍敏決，見事風生。

translations.literal: In youth he had talent and stratagem, was keen, bold, and quick in judgment, and grasped affairs as the wind rises.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed talent and strategic sense—sharp, resolute, and swift in judgment, seizing affairs the moment they arose.

sentences.zh: 以父任爲太廟齋郎。

translations.literal: By his father's position he became a Temple Acolyte.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's office he became a Temple Acolyte.

sentences.zh: 初調安州司理，監潤州酒務。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed judicial officer of An Prefecture and supervised the wine monopoly of Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as judicial officer of Anzhou and as supervisor of Runzhou's wine monopoly.

sentences.zh: 用薦改京官，監在京竹木務，擢提轄環慶路糧草，通判河間府。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was changed to capital official, supervised the capital bamboo-and-timber office, was promoted to commissioner of grain and fodder on the Huanqing circuit, and served as vice prefect of Hejian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for capital service, he oversaw the metropolitan bamboo-and-timber office, was promoted to commissioner for Huanqing circuit grain supplies, and served as vice prefect of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 以迕蔡京、童貫，換右列，由承議郎換莊宅副使，知信安軍，遷知霸州，爲遼國賀正副使。

translations.literal: For crossing Cai Jing and Tong Guan he was transferred to the military register; from Gentleman for Courteous Deportment he became Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Manors, governed Xin'an Army, was transferred to Bazhou, and served as deputy envoy congratulating the Liao on the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: After offending Cai Jing and Tong Guan he was shifted to military rank; from Gentleman for Courteous Deportment he became Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Manors, governed Xin'an Army and then Bazhou, and served as deputy envoy to the Liao New Year's court.

sentences.zh: 還，貫將連金人夾攻契丹，呼邈至私第，以語動之，使附己。

translations.literal: On his return, Guan was about to ally with the Jurchen in a pincer attack on the Khitan; he summoned Miao to his private residence, moved him with words, and wished him to attach himself to Guan.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Tong Guan planned a joint Jurchen attack on the Khitan; he summoned Miao privately, tried to win him over, and wanted him in his camp.

sentences.zh: 邈言契丹人未厭其主，貫懼邈有異議，即奏不俟對，令復任。

translations.literal: Miao said the Khitan people had not yet turned against their ruler; Guan, fearing Miao would dissent, memorialized that without awaiting audience he should resume his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Miao said the Khitan had not yet abandoned their ruler; Guan, fearing dissent, memorialized that Miao resume his post without awaiting audience.

sentences.zh: 邈上書言：「契丹不可滅，苟誤機事，願誅臣以謝邊吏。」

translations.literal: Miao memorialized: "The Khitan cannot be destroyed; if the opportunity is mishandled, I beg that Your Majesty execute me to answer the border officers."
translations.idiomatic: Miao wrote: "The Khitan cannot be destroyed; if policy errs, execute me to satisfy the frontier commanders."

sentences.zh: 都轉運使沈積中捃邈罪五十有三條，鞠治一無所得，乃以建神霄宮不如詔，免官。

translations.literal: The circuit transport commissioner Shen Jizhong gathered fifty-three charges against Miao; investigation found nothing, and he was dismissed for building the Divine Empyrean Palace contrary to edict.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Shen Jizhong compiled fifty-three charges; investigation found nothing, and Miao was dismissed for building the Divine Empyrean Palace contrary to edict.

sentences.zh: 久之，監在京染院，進都大提舉京西汴河堤岸。

translations.literal: After a long while he supervised the capital dye works and was promoted Grand Commissioner for the Bian River Embankments of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later he supervised the capital dye works and was promoted Grand Commissioner for the Bian River embankments west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 盜起浙東，改江、淮、兩浙制置司管當公事，改知嚴州，代還。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in eastern Zhe, he was changed to an administrative post in the Jiang-Huai and Two-Zhe Pacification Office, then made prefect of Yanzhou, and returned on completing his term.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in eastern Zhe he served in the Jiang-Huai and Two-Zhe Pacification Office, then as prefect of Yanzhou, and returned when his term ended.

sentences.zh: 貫欲以西師入燕，邈復語貫曰：「方臘小丑，一呼屠七州四十餘縣，竭數路之力而後能平之，殆天以此警公也，何可遽移之北乎？」

translations.literal: Guan wished to move western troops into Yan; Miao again said to Guan: "Fang La was a petty rebel; one cry and he slaughtered seven prefectures and more than forty counties—it took the strength of several circuits to subdue him. Heaven is perhaps warning you; how can you hastily shift forces north?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan wanted western troops for Yan; Miao warned: "Fang La was a petty rebel, yet one call laid waste to seven prefectures and forty-odd counties—it took several circuits to crush him. Heaven may be warning you; why rush troops north?"

sentences.zh: 因密教貫陰佐契丹以圖金人，貫不能用，乃乞致仕。

translations.literal: He secretly taught Guan to support the Khitan against the Jurchen in secret; Guan could not use this, and Miao asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly urged Guan to back the Khitan against the Jurchen; Guan would not listen, and Miao sought retirement.

sentences.zh: 貫收復燕山，奏邈知涿州，改易州，皆辭不赴。

translations.literal: When Guan recovered Yanshan, he memorialized Miao as prefect of Zhuozhou and then Yizhou; Miao declined both.
translations.idiomatic: After Guan recovered Yanshan he recommended Miao for Zhuozhou and Yizhou; Miao refused both posts.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「國家禍亂自茲始矣！」

translations.literal: He sighed: "The state's calamity begins from this!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed: "The realm's ruin begins here!"

sentences.zh: 金人犯京師，詔趣入見，邈慨然復起就道。

translations.literal: When the Jurchen attacked the capital, an edict hastened him to audience; Miao rose in high spirit and took the road again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchen struck the capital, an edict summoned him; Miao roused himself and set out once more.

sentences.zh: 既至，會姚平仲戰不利，京師震動，上不以時賜對，問禦敵奈何？

translations.literal: On arrival, as Yao Pingzhong's battle went badly and the capital was shaken, the emperor did not grant audience in time and asked how to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived as Yao Pingzhong's defeat shook the capital; the emperor delayed audience and asked how to repel the enemy.

sentences.zh: 邈言：「勝負兵家之常勢，陛下無過憂，第古未有和戰不定而能成功者。」

translations.literal: Miao said: "Victory and defeat are the constant lot of armies; Your Majesty need not over-worry—never in antiquity has success come when peace and war were undecided."
translations.idiomatic: Miao said: "Victory and defeat are the soldier's lot; Your Majesty need not despair—never has success come when war and peace waver together."

sentences.zh: 因言：「種師道宿將，有重名，二敵所畏。

translations.literal: He further said: "Zhong Shidao is a veteran of long standing with a great name, feared by both foes.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Zhong Shidao is a seasoned commander both enemies respect.

sentences.zh: 朝廷自主和議，而盡以諸道兵畀師道，視敵爲進退。

translations.literal: The court itself held to peace talks yet gave all troops of the circuits to Shidao, watching the enemy to advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: The court clung to peace while handing every circuit's troops to Shidao, letting the enemy dictate movement.

sentences.zh: 將在軍中，君命有所不受，使見可擊而進，勝固社稷之福；

translations.literal: The general in the army—imperial orders need not all be obeyed; let him strike when he sees opportunity; victory is the state's blessing;
translations.idiomatic: In camp the commander need not obey every order; let him attack when he sees chance—victory blesses the altars;

sentences.zh: 不勝，亦足使敵知吾將帥有以國爲任者。」

translations.literal: if not victorious, it is still enough to show the enemy that our commanders bear the state as their charge."
translations.idiomatic: and even defeat would show the enemy our generals answer to the realm."

sentences.zh: 上稱善，而耿南仲方主和議，不合，乃換右文殿修撰、京畿轉運使，辭不拜。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this, but Geng Nanzhong then led the peace party; disagreeing, Miao was made Drafting Attendant of the Right Hall for Literary Excellence and transport commissioner of the capital region, and he declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, but Geng Nanzhong led the peace faction; passed over, Miao was offered Drafting Attendant and capital transport commissioner and declined.

sentences.zh: 金人猶駐毛駝崗，乃以邈爲京城西壁守禦使。

translations.literal: The Jurchen still camped at Maotuo Ridge; Miao was made Defender of the western wall of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: With the Jurchen still at Maotuo Ridge, Miao was appointed defender of the capital's western wall.

sentences.zh: 邈言：「姚平仲敗績，而敵猶不敢留，是畏我也。

translations.literal: Miao said: "Yao Pingzhong was defeated, yet the enemy still dared not stay—that is fear of us.
translations.idiomatic: Miao said: "Yao Pingzhong lost, yet the enemy dared not remain—they fear us.

sentences.zh: 不以種師道再戰，已失機會；

translations.literal: Not to fight again under Zhong Shidao was already to lose opportunity;
translations.idiomatic: Not to fight again under Zhong Shidao was already to miss the chance;

sentences.zh: 尚可尾其行，及河半渡擊之，猶足爲後戒。」

translations.literal: one could still follow their march and strike when they were half across the river—enough to warn posterity."
translations.idiomatic: yet we could still pursue and strike them mid-river—a lesson for generations."

sentences.zh: 議復格。

translations.literal: Deliberation was again blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation was blocked again.

sentences.zh: 三上章致仕，不允。

translations.literal: Three times he memorialized to retire; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He thrice asked to retire; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 改主管馬軍公事、權樞密副都承旨，出爲河北西路制置使。

translations.literal: He was changed to director of cavalry affairs and acting deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and sent out as pacification commissioner of Hebei West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of cavalry affairs and acting deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then pacification commissioner of Hebei West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 以措置山西塘灣、屯田、弓箭手事。

translations.literal: He was charged with arranging the Shanxi ponds, garrison farms, and archer militia.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with the Shanxi ponds, garrison farms, and archer militia.

sentences.zh: 邈論塘灣不可爲，奪制置使，下遷提舉保甲，仍領措置司。

translations.literal: Miao argued the ponds could not be made; he was stripped of the pacification commission and demoted to commissioner for the militia, still heading the arrangements office.
translations.idiomatic: Miao argued the ponds were unworkable; stripped of the pacification post, he was demoted to militia commissioner while retaining the arrangements office.

sentences.zh: 又論不已，再奪觀察使，則金兵將及境矣。

translations.literal: He argued on without cease and was again stripped of the observer rank; then the Jin army was about to reach the border.
translations.idiomatic: He argued relentlessly and lost his observer rank; by then the Jin were nearing the frontier.

sentences.zh: 遂復舊官，守真定。

translations.literal: He was then restored to his former office and defended Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to his former rank and defended Zhending.

sentences.zh: 後二日，落階，拜青州觀察使，仍知府事。

translations.literal: Two days later he was reduced in rank, appointed observer of Qingzhou, and still governed the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he was demoted, appointed observer of Qingzhou, and still governed the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 邈始視事，兵不滿二千，錢不滿二百萬，自度無以拒敵，乃諭民出財，共爲死守。

translations.literal: When Miao first took office, troops numbered fewer than two thousand and cash fewer than two million; judging he could not resist the enemy, he urged the people to contribute wealth for a joint death defense.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he had fewer than two thousand troops and less than two million in cash; knowing he could not hold alone, he called on the people to fund a last stand.

sentences.zh: 民恃邈爲固，不數日，得錢十三萬貫、粟十一萬石，募民爲勇敢亦數千人。

translations.literal: The people trusted Miao as a bulwark; in a few days they raised one hundred thirty thousand strings of cash and one hundred ten thousand piculs of grain, and recruited several thousand brave militiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting Miao, within days they raised 130,000 strings of cash and 110,000 piculs of grain and several thousand militia.

sentences.zh: 而新集之兵皆無鬥志，金人至，邈乞師于宣撫副使劉韐，且間道走蠟書上聞，皆不報。

translations.literal: Yet the newly gathered troops had no fighting spirit; when the Jin came, Miao begged troops of the deputy commissioner Liu Ni and sent secret wax letters to the throne—all unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: The new levies lacked spirit; when the Jin came Miao begged Liu Ni for aid and sent secret dispatches—none answered.

sentences.zh: 城被圍，且戰且守，相持四旬。

translations.literal: The city was besieged; fighting and holding went on for forty days.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged, they fought and held for forty days.

sentences.zh: 城破，邈巷戰不克，將赴井，左右持之不得入。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Miao fought in the lanes without success; about to throw himself into a well, attendants held him back.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he fought in the alleys; barred from a well by his attendants, he could not drown himself.

sentences.zh: 斡離不脅邈拜，不拜，以火燎其鬚眉及兩髀，亦不顧，乃拘于燕山府。

translations.literal: Wolibu forced Miao to bow; he would not bow; they burned his beard, brows, and both thighs, yet he paid no heed, and he was detained in Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Wolibu demanded obeisance; Miao refused; they burned his beard, brows, and thighs—he did not flinch—and held him in Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 金人問曰：「集民兵擊我，謂我爲賊，何也？」

translations.literal: The Jurchen asked: "You gathered militia to strike us and called us bandits—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen asked: "You raised militia, called us bandits, and attacked us—why?"

sentences.zh: 邈曰：「汝負盟，所至掠吾金帛子女，何諱吾言敵？」

translations.literal: Miao said: "You broke the treaty; wherever you go you seize our gold, silk, and women—why should I shrink from calling you enemies?"
translations.idiomatic: Miao said: "You broke faith and seize gold, silk, and daughters wherever you march—why should I not call you enemies?"

sentences.zh: 不能屈。

translations.literal: They could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: They could not break him.

sentences.zh: 久之，欲以邈知滄州，笑而不答。

translations.literal: After a long while they wished to make Miao prefect of Cangzhou; he laughed and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Later they offered him Cangzhou; he laughed and was silent.

sentences.zh: 且說之曰：「天下強弱之勢安有常，特吾中國適逢其隙耳。

translations.literal: They also admonished him: "The world's strength and weakness have no constancy; it is only that our China happened upon a gap.
translations.idiomatic: They lectured him: "Power shifts; China merely met misfortune.

sentences.zh: 汝不以此時歸二帝及兩河地，歲取重幣如契丹，以爲長利，強尚可恃乎？」

translations.literal: If you do not now return the two emperors and the lands of the two He, taking heavy tribute yearly as with the Khitan for lasting profit, can strength still be relied upon?"
translations.idiomatic: Return the two emperors and the Two He, take tribute like the Khitan did—can you count on strength forever?"

sentences.zh: 金人諱其言，命邈被髮左衽，邈憤，詆毀甚力，金人撾其口，猶吮血噀之。

translations.literal: The Jurchen hated his words, ordered Miao to wear his hair loose and the left lapel; enraged, he reviled them fiercely; they beat his mouth, yet he still sucked blood and spat it at them.
translations.idiomatic: They ordered him to wear Jurchen dress; furious, he cursed them; they beat his mouth, and he spat blood in their faces.

sentences.zh: 翼日，自去發爲浮屠，金人大怒，遂遇害。

translations.literal: The next day he shaved his head as a monk; the Jurchen were greatly angered and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he tonsured himself as a monk; enraged, they executed him.

sentences.zh: 將死，顏色不變，南向再拜，端坐就戮，燕人爲之流涕。

translations.literal: Facing death his color did not change; he bowed twice to the south, sat upright and accepted execution, and men of Yan wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: At death his face did not change; he bowed south twice, sat upright to the blade, and men of Yan wept.

sentences.zh: 高宗贈昭化軍節度使，諡曰忠壯。

translations.literal: Gaozong posthumously enfeoffed him as military commissioner of Zhaohua Army and gave the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong posthumously made him military commissioner of Zhaohua with the posthumous name Loyal and Stalwart.

sentences.zh: 劉翊，靖康元年，以吉州防禦使爲真定府路都鈴轄。

translations.literal: Liu Yi—in the first year of Jingkang was made chief controller of Zhending prefecture circuit as defender of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi—in Jingkang's first year became chief controller of the Zhending circuit as defender of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 金人攻廣信、保州不克，遂越中山而攻真定。

translations.literal: The Jurchen attacked Guangxin and Baozhou without success, then passed Zhongshan to attack Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin failed against Guangxin and Baozhou, bypassed Zhongshan, and struck Zhending.

sentences.zh: 翊率衆晝夜搏戰城上。

translations.literal: Yi led the masses day and night battling on the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yi led the garrison in ceaseless fighting on the walls.

sentences.zh: 金兵初攻北壁，翊拒之，乃偽徙攻東城，宣撫使李邈復趣翊往應；

translations.literal: The Jin first attacked the north wall; Yi repelled them; they feigned a shift to the east wall, and the commissioner Li Miao again urged Yi to respond;
translations.idiomatic: The Jin first assaulted the north wall; Yi held them; they feigned an attack on the east, and Li Miao ordered Yi to shift there;

sentences.zh: 越再宿，潛移攻具還薄北城，衆攀堞而上，城遂陷。

translations.literal: after two nights they secretly moved siege engines back to press the north wall; the masses climbed the parapet and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: after two nights they secretly moved engines north again; soldiers scaled the wall and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 邈就執，翊猶集左右巷戰，已而稍亡去，翊顧其弟曰：「我大將也，其可受賊戮乎！」

translations.literal: Miao was seized; Yi still gathered his men for lane fighting; gradually they scattered; Yi said to his younger brother: "I am a great general—how can I suffer execution at the bandits' hands!"
translations.idiomatic: Miao was taken; Yi still fought in the alleys; as men fled he told his brother: "I am a great general—I will not die at bandits' hands!"

sentences.zh: 挺身潰圍欲出，諸門已爲敵所守，乃之孫氏山亭中，解絛自縊死。

translations.literal: He straightened his body, broke through the encirclement to escape; all gates were held by the enemy; he went to the Sun family hill pavilion, untied his sash, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He charged the encirclement; every gate was held; at the Sun family pavilion he hanged himself with his sash.

sentences.zh: 徐揆，衢州人。

translations.literal: Xu Kui was a man of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kui was from Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 游京師，入太學。

translations.literal: He traveled to the capital and entered the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the capital and entered the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，試開封府進士，爲舉首，未及大比而遭國難。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang he tested as a metropolitan graduate of Kaifeng Prefecture, placed first, and before the great examination met national calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang's first year he topped the Kaifeng metropolitan examination; before the palace exam calamity struck.

sentences.zh: 欽宗詣金營不歸，揆帥諸生扣南薰門，以書抵二酋，請車駕還闕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong went to the Jin camp and did not return, Kui led the students to knock at the Southern Fragrance Gate and sent a letter to the two chieftains asking that the imperial carriage return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong went to the Jin camp and did not return, Kui led students to the Southern Fragrance Gate and petitioned the two Jin commanders to send the emperor home.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「昔楚莊王入陳，欲以爲縣，申叔時諫，復封之。

translations.literal: The gist said: "Of old King Zhuang of Chu entered Chen and wished to make it a district; Shen Shushi remonstrated and he restored it as a fief.
translations.idiomatic: His letter recalled how King Zhuang of Chu wished to annex Chen until Shen Shushi persuaded him to restore Chen as a fief.

sentences.zh: 後世君子，莫不多叔時之善諫，楚子之從諫，千百歲之下，猶想其風采。

translations.literal: Later gentlemen all praised Shushi's good remonstrance and the king's heeding remonstrance; a thousand years on men still think of their bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages praised the minister's counsel and the king's heed—men still honor their example after a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 本朝失信大國，背盟致討，元帥之職也；

translations.literal: Our dynasty broke faith with a great state and broke the treaty to invite punishment—that is a marshal's duty;
translations.idiomatic: Our court broke faith with a great power and invited war—that is a commander's office;

sentences.zh: 郡城失守，社稷幾亡而存，元帥之德也；

translations.literal: the prefectural city was lost yet the altars nearly perished yet survived—that is a marshal's virtue;
translations.idiomatic: the capital nearly fell yet stood—that is your merit;

sentences.zh: 兵不血刃，市不易肆，生靈幾死而活，元帥之仁也；

translations.literal: arms did not bloody blades, markets did not change their stalls, the people nearly died yet lived—that is a marshal's benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: you took the city without slaughter and markets stayed open—the people lived—that is your mercy;

sentences.zh: 雖楚子存陳之功，未能有過。

translations.literal: even King Zhuang's merit in preserving Chen could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: even King Zhuang's mercy in sparing Chen cannot match this.

sentences.zh: 我皇帝親屈萬乘，兩造轅門，越在草莽，國中喁喁，跂望屬車之塵者屢矣。

translations.literal: Our emperor personally humbled the imperial carriage and went twice to the camp gate; he is now in the wilds, and within the state all murmur, often craning to the dust of the imperial train.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor humbled himself at your gates; he lingers in the wild while the realm strains toward the dust of his carriage.

sentences.zh: 道路之言，乃謂以金銀未足，故天子未返，揆竊惑之。

translations.literal: Roadside talk says that because gold and silver are not enough the Son of Heaven has not returned; Kui is privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor says gold and silver alone detain him; I cannot believe it.

sentences.zh: 今國家帑藏既空．編民一妾婦之飾，一器用之微，無不輸之公上。

translations.literal: Now the state treasury is empty; of commoners, even a concubine's ornament or the least utensil—none is not rendered to the government.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury is empty; every trinket of the people has gone to the state.

sentences.zh: 商賈絕跡，不來京邑，區區豈足以償需索之數。

translations.literal: Merchants have ceased coming to the capital; how can the paltry sum satisfy their demands?
translations.idiomatic: Merchants no longer come to the capital—how can scraps satisfy your demands?

sentences.zh: 有存社稷之德，活生靈之仁，而以金帛之故，留質君父。

translations.literal: To have the merit of preserving the altars and the benevolence of saving the people yet detain the ruler and father for gold and silk—
translations.idiomatic: To save the realm yet hold the emperor for gold—

sentences.zh: 是猶愛人之子弟，而辱其父祖，與不愛無擇，元帥必不爲也。

translations.literal: it is like loving a man's sons yet shaming his father and grandfather; it is no different from not loving—surely the marshal would not do this.
translations.idiomatic: is like honoring sons while shaming their fathers—you would not do this.

sentences.zh: 願推惻隱之心，存始終之惠，反其君父，班師振旅，緩以時日，使求之四方，然後遣使人奉獻，則楚封陳之功不足道也。」

translations.literal: I wish you to extend compassionate heart, preserve beginning-to-end grace, return our ruler and father, withdraw the army in good order, allow time, let us seek from the four quarters, then send envoys with tribute—then the merit of Chu in enfeoffing Chen would not be worth mentioning."
translations.idiomatic: Extend mercy, return our emperor, withdraw in order, grant time to gather tribute from the four quarters—then Chen's restoration would seem a small kindness."

sentences.zh: 二酋見書，使以馬載揆至軍詰難，揆厲聲抗論，爲所殺。

translations.literal: The two chieftains saw the letter, had Kui carried on horseback to the camp to interrogate him; Kui argued loudly in resistance and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The two commanders read the letter, had Kui brought to camp on horseback for questioning; he answered fiercely and was killed.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，追錄死節，詔贈宣教郎，而官其後。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan his death in loyalty was recorded posthumously; an edict enfeoffed him as Instructor in the Edict and appointed his descendants to office.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan's second year the court honored his martyrdom, posthumously promoting him to Instructor in the Edict and granting office to his kin.

sentences.zh: 陳遘，字亨伯，其先自江寧徙永州。

translations.literal: Chen Gou, style name Hengbo—his ancestors moved from Jiangning to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gou, styled Hengbo, came of a family that had moved from Jiangning to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 知莘縣，爲治有績，魏尹蔣之奇、馮京、許將交薦之。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Xin County his governance had achievement; the Wei prefects Jiang Zhiqi, Feng Jing, and Xu Jiang jointly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Xin County he governed well; Jiang Zhiqi, Feng Jing, and Xu Jiang of Wei prefecture all recommended him.

sentences.zh: 知雍丘縣，徽宗將以爲御史，而遭父祐甫憂。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Yongqiu County the emperor was about to make him censor when he met mourning for his father Youfu.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Yongqiu, he was slated for the censorate when his father Youfu died.

sentences.zh: 畢喪，爲廣西轉運判官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became transport judge of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he became transport judge of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 蔡京啟蠻徭地，建平、從、允三州，遘言：「蠻人幸安靜，輕擾以兆釁，不可。」

translations.literal: Cai Jing opened Man and Yao lands, establishing Ping, Cong, and Yun prefectures; Gou said: "The Man are fortunate in quiet; lightly disturbing them will breed trouble—it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing opened tribal lands and founded three prefectures; Gou warned: "The tribes prize peace—provoke them and trouble follows."

sentences.zh: 京惡之，以他事罷歸。

translations.literal: Jing hated this and dismissed him on another matter.
translations.idiomatic: Jing resented him and removed him on a pretext.

sentences.zh: 旋知商州、興元府，入爲駕部、金部員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he governed Shangzhou and Xingyuan Prefecture and entered the capital as secretary in the Ministry of Carriages and of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He soon governed Shangzhou and Xingyuan and entered the capital as a Ministry of Revenue secretary.

sentences.zh: 張商英得政，用爲左司員外郎。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shangying took power he was used as left-department vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhang Shangying he served as left-department vice director.

sentences.zh: 俄擢給事中，會商英免相。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to drafting attendant; Shangying was removed from the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made drafting attendant; then Shangying fell from power.

sentences.zh: 蔡薿攝封駁，力沮止之，遘懼，請外。

translations.literal: Cai Yu acted as seal controller and strongly blocked it; Gou feared and asked for an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yu blocked the appointment; Gou feared him and sought a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 以直秘閣爲河北轉運使，加直龍圖閣，徙陝西。

translations.literal: As Direct Secretariat Attendant he was Hebei transport commissioner, added Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion, and moved to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: As Direct Secretariat Attendant he became Hebei transport commissioner, gained the Dragon Diagram title, and was transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 召還京師，而蔡京復相，再使河北，徙淮南。

translations.literal: Recalled to the capital, when Cai Jing returned to office he was again sent to Hebei, then to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, then sent again to Hebei and Huainan when Cai Jing returned.

sentences.zh: 帝將易置發運使，命選諸道計臣有閥閱者，執政以遘言，京曰：「職卑不可用，願更選。」

translations.literal: The emperor was about to replace the transport commissioner and ordered selection of circuit accountants of good family; the chief ministers named Gou; Jing said: "The post is too low—choose another."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sought a new transport chief; ministers named Gou; Jing said his rank was too low.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「可除集英殿修撰使往。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "He may be made Drafting Attendant of the Hall of Assembled Eminence and sent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Promote him to Drafting Attendant of the Hall of Assembled Eminence and send him."

sentences.zh: 京乃不敢言。

translations.literal: Jing then dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Jing held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 遂爲副使，未幾，升爲使。

translations.literal: He became deputy commissioner and soon was promoted commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became deputy commissioner, then commissioner.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方督綱餉，運渠壅澀，遘使決呂城、陳公兩塘達于渠。

translations.literal: The court was pressing grain transport; the canal was silted; Gou had the Lücheng and Chen'gong ponds opened to the channel.
translations.idiomatic: With grain transport urgent and canals choked, he opened the Lücheng and Chen'gong ponds to the channel.

sentences.zh: 漕路甫通，而朱勔花石綱塞道，官舟不得行。

translations.literal: The transport route had just opened when Zhu Mian's Flower-and-Stone convoys blocked the way and official boats could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: The route had barely opened when Zhu Mian's tribute convoys blocked official traffic.

sentences.zh: 遘捕系其人，而上章自劾。

translations.literal: Gou arrested the men and memorialized impeaching himself.
translations.idiomatic: Gou arrested the offenders and memorialized against himself.

sentences.zh: 帝爲黥勔人，進遘徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: The emperor tattooed Mian's men and promoted Gou to Awaiting Drafting Attendant of the Huixian Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor branded Mian's men and promoted Gou to Awaiting Drafting Attendant of the Huixian Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年冬，方臘亂，詔以屬遘。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xuanhe, Fang La rebelled; an edict placed this under Gou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe's second winter Fang La rebelled; Gou was put in charge.

sentences.zh: 遘言：「臘始起青溪，衆不及千，今脅從已過萬，又有蘇州石生、歸安陸行兒，皆聚党應之。

translations.literal: Gou said: "La first rose at Qingxi with fewer than a thousand; now coerced followers exceed ten thousand; Su Shisheng of Suzhou and Lu Xing'er of Gui'an also gather bands in response.
translations.idiomatic: Gou reported: "La began with under a thousand at Qingxi; coerced followers now exceed ten thousand; others rally in Suzhou and Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 東南兵弱勢單，士不習戰，必未能滅賊。

translations.literal: Southeastern troops are few and weak, soldiers unused to war—they surely cannot destroy the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Southeastern forces are weak and untrained—they cannot destroy the rebels alone.

sentences.zh: 願發京畿兵、鼎澧槍盾手，兼程以來，庶幾蜂起愚民。

translations.literal: I wish to send capital troops and Ding-Li spear-and-shield men by forced marches; perhaps the swarming foolish people will not spread further.
translations.idiomatic: Send capital troops and Ding-Li spearmen at forced march lest the revolt spread.

sentences.zh: 不至滋蔓。」

translations.literal: They will not spread further."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the uprising may be contained."

sentences.zh: 帝悉行其言。

translations.literal: The emperor fully carried out his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 加龍圖閣直學士，經制七路，治于杭。

translations.literal: He was added Direct Dragon Diagram Academician, commissioner of seven circuits, with headquarters at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Direct Dragon Diagram Academician, commissioner over seven circuits, based at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時縣官用度百出，遘創議度公私出納，量增其贏，號「經製錢」。

translations.literal: At that time official expenses were myriad; Gou devised measuring public and private receipts and increasing the surplus, called "commissioner funds."
translations.idiomatic: With expenses soaring, he devised "commissioner funds" by measuring public and private intake and increasing surcharges.

sentences.zh: 其後總制使翁彥國仿其式，號「總製錢」。

translations.literal: Later the chief commissioner Weng Yanguo imitated the form, called "aggregate funds."
translations.idiomatic: Later Weng Yanguo copied the scheme as "aggregate funds."

sentences.zh: 于是天下至今有「經總製錢」名，自兩人始也。

translations.literal: Thus to this day there is the name "commissioner-aggregate funds," beginning with these two men.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the lasting name "commissioner-aggregate funds," from these two men.

sentences.zh: 又言：「妖賊陵暴州縣，唯搜求官吏，恣行殺戮。

translations.literal: He also said: "Demon bandits overrun prefectures and counties, only seeking officials, indulging in slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "The rebels ravage counties, hunting officials and slaughtering without mercy.

sentences.zh: 往往斷截支體，探取肺肝，或熬以鼎油，或射以勁矢，備極慘毒，不廠怨心。

translations.literal: Often they sever limbs and take lungs and livers, or boil in cauldrons of oil, or shoot with strong arrows—extreme cruelty, never sated.
translations.idiomatic: They mutilate bodies, boil victims in oil, shoot them with heavy arrows—cruelty without end.

sentences.zh: 蓋貪污嗜利之人，倚法侵牟騷動，不知藝極。

translations.literal: Greedy men who covet profit, relying on law to extort and stir trouble, know no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy officials who extort by law have no limit.

sentences.zh: 積有不平之氣，結于民心，一旦乘勢如此，可爲悲痛！

translations.literal: Long-gathered injustice binds the people's hearts; one day they seize the moment thus—how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Years of injustice bred this rage—how tragic.

sentences.zh: 此風不除，必更生事。

translations.literal: If this wind is not removed, trouble will surely arise again.
translations.idiomatic: Unless this is checked, rebellion will rise again.

sentences.zh: 臣願采摭官吏奸贓尚仍舊習者，按治以聞，乞重置于理。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to gather officials guilty of corruption who still follow old habits, investigate and report, and beg heavy punishment by law."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to investigate corrupt officials still at their old ways and punish them severely."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 又進學士，凡所施置，以御筆先下。

translations.literal: He was further promoted academician; whatever he set in place came down by imperial brush first.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted again, his measures came preceded by imperial brush orders.

sentences.zh: 于是劾越州王仲薿糾市民造金茶器，減直買軍糧券，而以私錢取之，仲薿坐黜。

translations.literal: Thus he impeached Wang Zhong'ai of Yuezhou for forcing townspeople to make gold tea vessels, discounting military grain tickets and taking private money—Zhong'ai was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Wang Zhong'ai of Yue for extorting gold tea sets and cheating grain tickets; Zhong'ai was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 杭經巨寇後，河渠堙窒，邦人以水潦爲病。

translations.literal: Hangzhou, after great bandits, had clogged waterways; the people suffered floods.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion Hangzhou's waterways were choked and floods plagued the people.

sentences.zh: 前守數請于朝，皆以勞費輟役。

translations.literal: Former prefects several times asked the court; all halted work as too costly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier prefects had begged the court for dredging; cost always stopped them.

sentences.zh: 遘以冬月檄真、揚、潤、楚諸郡，凡守閘綱卒，悉集治所。

translations.literal: Gou in winter month ordered Zhen, Yang, Run, and Chu—all gate-keeping convoy soldiers to gather at the seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he summoned gate guards from Zhen, Yang, Run, and Chu to the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 先是，當閉閘，群卒無以食，率凍餓不自聊。

translations.literal: Before, when gates were to close, the soldiers had no food and mostly froze and starved in misery.
translations.idiomatic: Those soldiers had often starved when gates closed for winter.

sentences.zh: 聞命，相率呼舞以來者二千人，用其力治河，不兩月畢，杭人利焉。

translations.literal: Hearing the order, about two thousand came dancing and shouting; their labor cleared the river in less than two months—Hangzhou profited.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand came gladly; in under two months the river was cleared to Hangzhou's benefit.

sentences.zh: 徙河北都轉運使，進延康殿學士，曆知中山、真定、河間府。

translations.literal: He was moved to chief transport commissioner of Hebei, promoted academician of the Yankang Hall, and successively governed Zhongshan, Zhending, and Hejian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He became Hebei chief transport commissioner, Yankang academician, and governed Zhongshan, Zhending, and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 欽宗立，加資政殿學士，積官至光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Qinzong ascended he was added academician of the Zizheng Hall, accumulating to Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qinzong he rose to Zizheng academician and Grandee of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 復爲真定，又徙中山。

translations.literal: He was again at Zhending, then moved to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Zhending, then moved to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 金人再至，遘冒圍入城，堅壁拒守。

translations.literal: When the Jin came again, Gou broke through the encirclement into the city and firmly walled to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin returned, Gou broke through the siege into the city and held firm.

sentences.zh: 詔康王領天下大元帥，命遘爲兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: An edict made the Prince of Kang grand marshal of all under Heaven; Gou was made army-and-horse marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kang was made grand marshal; Gou was made army-and-horse marshal.

sentences.zh: 受圍半年，外無援師。

translations.literal: Besieged half a year, there was no relief from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged half a year, no relief came.

sentences.zh: 京都既陷，割兩河求和。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, the two He were ceded to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, the Two He were ceded for peace.

sentences.zh: 遘弟光祿卿適至中山，臨城諭旨，遘遙語之曰：「主辱臣死。

translations.literal: Gou's younger brother, Chamberlain for Imperial Sacrifices Shi, reached Zhongshan; approaching the wall he announced the edict; Gou called from afar: "The ruler is shamed and ministers must die.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shi arrived with the edict; Gou shouted from the wall: "The ruler is shamed—ministers must die.

sentences.zh: 吾兄弟平居以名義自處，寧當賣國家爲囚孥乎？」

translations.literal: We brothers in ordinary times hold ourselves by reputation—how could we sell the state and become captives?"
translations.idiomatic: We live by honor—how could we sell the realm and become prisoners?"

sentences.zh: 適泣曰：「兄但盡力，勿以弟爲念。」

translations.literal: Shi wept: "Elder brother, only strive with all strength; do not think of me."
translations.idiomatic: Shi wept: "Brother, fight on—forget me."

sentences.zh: 遘呼總管使盡括城中兵擊賊，總管辭，遂斬以徇。

translations.literal: Gou called the chief controller to gather all troops in the city to strike the bandits; the controller declined and was beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Gou ordered the chief controller to rally every soldier; the man refused and Gou beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 又呼步將沙振往。

translations.literal: He also called the infantry commander Sha Zhen to go.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent infantry commander Sha Zhen.

sentences.zh: 振素有勇名，亦固辭，遘固遣之。

translations.literal: Zhen had long had a brave name yet firmly declined; Gou insisted on sending him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, famed for courage, refused; Gou insisted.

sentences.zh: 振怒且懼，潛衷刃入府。

translations.literal: Zhen, angry and afraid, secretly hid a blade and entered the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Angry and afraid, Zhen hid a blade and entered the hall.

sentences.zh: 遘妾定奴責其輒入，振立殺之，遂害遘于堂，及其子錫並僕妾十七人。

translations.literal: Gou's concubine Dingnu rebuked him for entering rashly; Zhen immediately killed her, then killed Gou in the hall, his son Xi, and seventeen servants and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Concubine Dingnu scolded his intrusion; he killed her, then Gou in the hall, his son Xi, and seventeen household members.

sentences.zh: 長子钜以官淮南獲免。

translations.literal: The eldest son Ju, holding office in Huainan, escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Ju, serving in Huainan, survived.

sentences.zh: 振出，帳下卒噪而前曰：「大敵臨城，汝安得殺吾父？」

translations.literal: Zhen went out; the tent soldiers clamored forward: "The great enemy is at the walls—how dare you kill our father?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen fled; soldiers cried: "The enemy is at the gates—how dare you kill our leader?"

sentences.zh: 執而捽裂之，身首無餘。

translations.literal: They seized and tore him apart; body and head were not left.
translations.idiomatic: They seized and tore him limb from limb.

sentences.zh: 城中無主，乃開門出降。

translations.literal: With no one in charge in the city, they opened the gates and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Leaderless, the city opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 金人入見其屍曰：「南朝忠臣也。」

translations.literal: The Jin, seeing his corpse, said: "A loyal minister of the Southern Court."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin, seeing his body, said: "A loyal minister of the Song."

sentences.zh: 斂而葬諸鐵柱寺。

translations.literal: They gathered and buried him at the Iron Pillar Temple.
translations.idiomatic: They buried him at the Iron Pillar Temple.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，贈特進。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan he was posthumously promoted to Special Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan he was posthumously made Special Grandee.

sentences.zh: 遘性孝友，爲人寬厚長者。

translations.literal: Gou's nature was filial and friendly; as a man he was generous and a elder of long virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was filial, friendly, generous, and long-tempered.

sentences.zh: 任部刺史二十年，每出行郡邑，必焚香祈天，願不逢貪濁吏。

translations.literal: For twenty years as prefectural inspector, whenever he went out to a county seat he burned incense and prayed Heaven he might not meet greedy and corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years as prefect he burned incense whenever he toured a county, praying not to meet corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 嘗薦王安中、呂頤浩、張愨、謝克家、何鑄，後皆至公輔，世以爲知人。

translations.literal: He once recommended Wang Anzhong, Lü Yihao, Zhang Kai, Xie Kejia, and He Zhu—all later reached high office; the age deemed him a knower of men.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Wang Anzhong, Lü Yihao, Zhang Kai, Xie Kejia, and He Zhu—all later reached high office; men called him a judge of talent.

sentences.zh: 適由開封少尹、衛尉少卿至光祿卿。

translations.literal: Shi rose from Vice Magistrate of Kaifeng and Vice Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia to Chamberlain for Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Shi rose from Kaifeng vice magistrate to Chamberlain for Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 是役也，金人執之以北。

translations.literal: In this campaign the Jin seized him and took him north.
translations.idiomatic: In this war the Jin seized him and took him north.

sentences.zh: 後十年，死于雲中。

translations.literal: Ten years later he died in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yunzhong ten years later.

sentences.zh: 趙不試

translations.literal: Zhao Bushi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bushi.

sentences.zh: 趙不試，太宗六世孫。

translations.literal: Zhao Bushi was a sixth-generation descendant of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bushi was a sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，通判相州，尋權州事兼主管真定府路經略安撫公事。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe he was vice prefect of Xiangzhou and soon held the prefecture while directing Zhending circuit pacification and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xuanhe he was vice prefect of Xiangzhou, then governed it and directed Zhending pacification.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，知相州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan he was made prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan's first year he became prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，汪伯彥既去相，金人執其子似，遣來割地，似至相，不試固守不下。

translations.literal: At first, after Wang Boyan left Xiang, the Jin seized his son Si and sent him to cede territory; when Si reached Xiang, Bushi firmly held and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Boyan left, the Jin took his son Si hostage to demand territory; at Xiang, Bushi refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，金人大入。

translations.literal: The next year the Jin entered in force.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Jin invaded in force.

sentences.zh: 州久被圍，軍民無固志，不試謂之曰：「今城中食乏，外援不至。

translations.literal: The prefecture had long been besieged; soldiers and people lacked firm will; Bushi said to them: "Now food in the city is scarce and outside aid does not come.
translations.idiomatic: Long besieged, morale failed; Bushi told them: "Food is scarce and no aid comes.

sentences.zh: 不試，宗子也，義不降，計將安出？」

translations.literal: Bushi, as a clansman, in righteousness will not surrender—what plan shall we take?"
translations.idiomatic: I am imperial kin and will not surrender—what shall we do?"

sentences.zh: 衆不應。

translations.literal: The crowd did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The people were silent.

sentences.zh: 不試知事不可爲，遂登城與金人約勿殺，許之。

translations.literal: Bushi knew the matter could not be done; he ascended the wall and agreed with the Jin not to kill; they assented.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no hope, he climbed the wall and bargained that the Jin spare the people; they agreed.

sentences.zh: 既啟門，乃納其家井中，然後以身赴井，命提轄官實以土。

translations.literal: When the gate was opened he put his family in a well, then himself entered the well and ordered the controller to fill it with earth.
translations.idiomatic: When the gates opened he cast his family into a well, then followed and ordered it filled with earth.

sentences.zh: 州人皆免于死。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture all escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: The people were spared.

sentences.zh: 趙令峸

translations.literal: Zhao Lingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lingcheng.

sentences.zh: 趙令峸，燕懿王玄孫，安定郡王令衿兄也。

translations.literal: Zhao Lingcheng was a great-grandson of Prince Yiyi of Yan; he was the elder brother of Prince Anding Lingqin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lingcheng was a great-grandson of Prince Yiyi of Yan and elder brother of Prince Anding Lingqin.

sentences.zh: 初名令裨。

translations.literal: At first his name was Lingpi.
translations.idiomatic: He was first named Lingpi.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，仕至鄂州通判，領兵戍武昌。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan he reached vice prefect of Ezhou and led troops garrisoning Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan he was vice prefect of Ezhou, garrisoning Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 賊閻瑾犯黃州，縱掠而去。

translations.literal: The bandit Yan Jin invaded Huangzhou and plundered as he left.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Yan Jin raided Huangzhou and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 令峸渡江存撫之，黃人乃安。

translations.literal: Lingcheng crossed the river to comfort them; the people of Huang were then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Lingcheng crossed the river to reassure the people; Huangzhou calmed.

sentences.zh: 李綱言于上，擢直龍圖閣、知黃州，賜今名。

translations.literal: Li Gang spoke to the throne; he was promoted Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion and made prefect of Huangzhou, and given his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang recommended him; he was made prefect of Huangzhou with his present name.

sentences.zh: 奉詔修城，凡六月而畢。

translations.literal: By imperial order he repaired the walls; in all six months it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to repair the walls, he finished in six months.

sentences.zh: 賊張遇過城下，招令峸。

translations.literal: Before long, the bandit Zhang Yu passed below the city and summoned Lingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the bandit Zhang Yu passed the walls and summoned Lingcheng.

sentences.zh: 度不能拒，出城見之，遇飲以酒，一舉而盡，曰：「固知飲此必死，願勿殺軍民。」

translations.literal: Judging he could not resist, he went out to see Yu; Yu gave him wine; he drained it at one draft and said: "I know well that drinking this means death—only spare soldiers and people."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not hold, he went out; Yu offered wine; he drank it off and said: "I know this is death—spare my soldiers and people."

sentences.zh: 遇驚曰：「先以此試公耳。」

translations.literal: Yu said in alarm: "I only tested you first."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said in alarm: "I was only testing you."

sentences.zh: 更取毒酒沃地，地裂有聲，乃引軍去。

translations.literal: He took more poisoned wine and poured it on the ground; the ground cracked with sound, and he led the army away.
translations.idiomatic: He poured poisoned wine on the ground; the earth cracked audibly, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁進、李成兵迭至，俱擊卻之。

translations.literal: Before long, the armies of Ding Jin and Li Cheng came in turn; all were beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ding Jin and Li Cheng attacked in turn; he repulsed them both.

sentences.zh: 叛將孔彥舟又引兵圍城，率民兵固守，凡六日乃解。

translations.literal: The rebel general Kong Yanzhou again led troops to besiege the city; Lingcheng led militia to hold firm; in six days it was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Kong Yanzhou besieged the city again; Lingcheng held with militia until the siege lifted after six days.

sentences.zh: 三年，以內艱去，詔起復。

translations.literal: In the third year he left on inner mourning; an edict recalled him to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he left for mourning; an edict ordered him back to duty.

sentences.zh: 時金人聞孟太后在南昌，欲邀之，徑犯黃州。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin heard Empress Dowager Meng was at Nanchang and wished to intercept her; they struck Huangzhou directly.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin learned Empress Dowager Meng was at Nanchang and marched straight on Huangzhou to seize her.

sentences.zh: 令峸已還在道，郡卒得金人木笴鑿頭箭，浮江告急。

translations.literal: Lingcheng was still on the road; county soldiers got Jin wooden-bolt head-piercing arrows floating on the river and reported urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Lingcheng was still en route when garrison troops found Jin arrows on the river and brought word of attack.

sentences.zh: 令峸疾趨，夜半入城。

translations.literal: Lingcheng hurried; at midnight he entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: He raced back and entered the city at midnight.

sentences.zh: 金人力攻，翼日城陷。

translations.literal: The Jin pressed the attack fiercely; the next day the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin assaulted fiercely; the city fell the next day.

sentences.zh: 金人欲降之，大罵不屈，酌以酒，揮之不肯飲，又衣以戰袍，曰：「我豈當服！」

translations.literal: The Jin wished to make him surrender; he cursed and would not yield; they poured wine; he waved it away and would not drink; they clothed him in a battle robe; he said: "How should I wear this!"
translations.idiomatic: They tried to break him; he cursed and refused wine; they dressed him in a battle robe—"How should I wear this?"

sentences.zh: 金人曰：「趙使君何堅執膝？」

translations.literal: The Jin said: "Why is Commissioner Zhao so stubborn about bending the knee?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked why he would not kneel.

sentences.zh: 曰：「但當拜祖宗，豈能拜犬彘！」

translations.literal: He said: "One should only bow to ancestors—how could one bow to dogs and swine!"
translations.idiomatic: He said: "I bow only to ancestors—not to dogs and swine!"

sentences.zh: 金人怒鞭之，流血被面，罵不絕口而死。

translations.literal: The Jin angrily flogged him; blood covered his face; cursing without cease he died.
translations.idiomatic: They flogged him until blood covered his face; he cursed them to the end and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈徽猷閣待制，諡曰湣忠。

translations.literal: When the matter was heard, he was posthumously made Awaiting Drafting Attendant of the Huixian Pavilion; posthumous title Minzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Huixian Attendant with the posthumous name Steadfast in Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 州人乞立廟，從之。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture begged to erect a temple; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The people petitioned for a temple; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，城破，都監王達、判官吳源、巡檢劉卓，皆以不屈死焉。

translations.literal: At first when the city fell, Controller Wang Da, Administrator Wu Yuan, and Inspector Liu Zhuo all died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Controller Wang Da, Administrator Wu Yuan, and Inspector Liu Zhuo also died refusing surrender.

sentences.zh: 唐重，字聖任，眉州彭山人。

translations.literal: Tang Chong, style name Shengren, was a native of Pengshan in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Chong, styled Shengren, was from Pengshan in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 少有大志。

translations.literal: In youth he had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he burned with ambition.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the third year of Daguan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Daguan's third year.

sentences.zh: 徽宗親策士，問以制禮作樂，重對曰：「事親從兄，爲仁義禮樂之實。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong personally examined scholars and asked about regulating rites and making music; Chong answered: "Serving parents and following elder brothers are the substance of benevolence, righteousness, rites, and music.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong examined candidates on rites and music; Chong answered: "Filial piety and brotherhood are the substance of ritual—not mere ceremony.

sentences.zh: 陛下以神考爲父，哲宗爲兄，盍亦推原仁義之實而已，何以製作爲？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty takes Emperor Shenzong as father and Emperor Zhezong as elder brother—why not extend the substance of benevolence and righteousness, and what need for mere regulation?"
translations.idiomatic: You honor Shenzong as father and Zhezong as brother—live their benevolence; why fixate on formal regulation?"

sentences.zh: 授蜀州司理參軍，改成都府府學教授，知懷安軍金堂縣，授辟雍錄。

translations.literal: He was appointed judicial officer of Shu Prefecture, changed to professor of the Chengdu prefectural school, governed Jintang County in Huai'an Army, and was made Recorder of the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Shu judicial officer, Chengdu professor, magistrate of Jintang, and Imperial College recorder.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷以拓土爲功，邊帥爭興利以徼賞，凡蜀東西、夔峽路及荊湖、廣南，皆誘近邊蕃夷獻其地之不可耕者，謂之納土，因置州縣，所至騷然。

translations.literal: Before this the court took expanding territory as merit; frontier commanders vied to create profit to seek reward; throughout eastern and western Shu, the Kuizhou gorge route, Jinghu, and Guangnan all lured nearby tribes to offer uncultivable land called "presenting territory," then set up prefectures and counties—wherever they went there was turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The court prized territorial expansion; frontier generals bribed tribes to "present" barren land and founded prefectures—everywhere brought unrest.

sentences.zh: 重以其利害白之宰相，因是薦之，召對。

translations.literal: Chong reported the harm and gain to the chancellor and was recommended; summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: He explained the policy's harm to the chancellor, was recommended, and was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部員外郎、左司郎官、起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was moved to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, left-department director, and Attendant for Drafting of the Rise and Fall.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of Personnel, left-department director, and drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 金人入京師，重言：「開邊之禍，起于童貫，故金人以貫爲禍首。

translations.literal: When the Jin entered the capital, Chong said: "The calamity of opening the frontier began with Tong Guan—therefore the Jin take Guan as the chief culprit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin took the capital he said: "Opening the frontier began with Tong Guan—the Jin name him chief culprit.

sentences.zh: 若斬貫首，遣人傳送于金，尚可緩兵。」

translations.literal: If Guan's head is cut off and men are sent to deliver it to the Jin, troops might still be slowed."
translations.idiomatic: Execute Guan and send his head to the Jin—perhaps they will pause."

sentences.zh: 或獻議遠避，重聞衛士語，以告于朝，始定守城之計。

translations.literal: Some offered the plan of fleeing far; Chong heard the guards' talk and reported to the court—only then was the plan to defend the city settled.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged flight; Chong reported what the guards said, and the court settled on defense.

sentences.zh: 擢右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 時宰執各主和戰二議，重上疏乞命其廷辨得失。

translations.literal: Chief ministers each held peace or war; Chong memorialized begging command debate in court of gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: With court divided on war and peace, he asked for open debate.

sentences.zh: 金人要求金帛，中書侍郎王孝迪下令，有匿金銀者死，許人告。

translations.literal: The Jin demanded gold and silk; Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Xiaodi issued orders—whoever hid gold and silver would die; informing was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin demanded gold; Wang Xiaodi ordered death for hoarders and rewards for informers.

sentences.zh: 重曰：「如此，則子得以告父，弟得以告兄，奴婢得以告主矣，豈初政所宜？」

translations.literal: Chong said: "Thus sons may report fathers, younger brothers elder brothers, slaves and maidservants their masters—is this fit for a new reign?"
translations.idiomatic: He protested: "Sons will denounce fathers, slaves their masters—is this how a new reign should begin?"

sentences.zh: 即與御史抗論，乃止。

translations.literal: He joined the censors in argument and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He and the censors protested until the order was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 又累疏乞斬蔡京父子以謝天下。

translations.literal: He again several times memorialized begging execution of Cai Jing and his sons to answer the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly demanded execution of Cai Jing and his sons.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書舍人，詞命多所繳奏。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat; many edicts he returned with objection.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to drafting attendant, he blocked many edicts.

sentences.zh: 又言：「近世不次用人，其間致身宰輔，有未嘗一日出國門者。

translations.literal: He also said: "In recent times men are appointed out of order; among them some reach the chief ministry who have never in one day left the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: He warned: "Men leap to high office without ever leaving the capital.

sentences.zh: 乞先補外，以爲之倡。」

translations.literal: I beg first to send them outside as a model."
translations.idiomatic: Send them to the provinces first—as an example."

sentences.zh: 上開納，而宰相執奏以爲不可。

translations.literal: The emperor was receptive, but the chief ministers held memorials that it could not be.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; the chancellors blocked it.

sentences.zh: 明日，台諫皆得罪，重落職知同州。

translations.literal: The next day the censors all suffered punishment; Chong was demoted to govern Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the remonstrators were punished; Chong was sent to govern Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 金人已陷晉、絳，將及同。

translations.literal: The Jin had already taken Jin and Jiang and were about to reach Tong.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin had taken Jin and Jiang and were nearing Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 重度不能守，乃開門縱州人使出，自以殘兵數百守城，以示必死。

translations.literal: Chong judged he could not hold; he opened the gates and let the people of the prefecture leave; he himself with several hundred remnant troops guarded the city to show certain death.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not hold, he opened the gates for the people and kept a few hundred men to show he would die defending.

sentences.zh: 金人疑有備，不復渡河而返。

translations.literal: The Jin suspected preparations and did not cross the river again but returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin suspected a trap, did not cross the river, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 降詔獎諭，擢天章閣待制。

translations.literal: An edict praised and promoted him to Awaiting Drafting Attendant of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him and made him Awaiting Drafting Attendant of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns.

sentences.zh: 先是，陝西宣撫使范致虛提五路兵勤王，至陝州。

translations.literal: Before this, Shaanxi Commissioner Fan Zhixu led five circuits' troops to aid the king and reached Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fan Zhixu had led five circuits toward the capital and reached Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 重遺致虛書，言：「中都倚秦兵爲爪牙，諸夏恃京師爲根本。

translations.literal: Chong sent Zhixu a letter saying: "The central capital relies on Qin troops as claws and teeth; all regions rely on the capital as root.
translations.idiomatic: Chong wrote Fan Zhixu: "The capital relies on Qin armies; the realm relies on the capital.

sentences.zh: 今京城圍久，人無鬥志，若五路之師逡巡未進，則所以爲爪牙者不足恃，而根本搖矣。

translations.literal: Now the capital is long besieged and men lack fighting will; if the five circuits' armies hesitate and do not advance, the claws and teeth cannot be relied on and the root is shaken.
translations.idiomatic: With the capital long besieged, if your armies linger, the root itself shakes.

sentences.zh: 然潰卒爲梗，關中公私之積已盡；

translations.literal: Yet routed soldiers are an obstacle; public and private stores in Guanzhong are exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Routed troops block the roads; Guanzhong's stores are empty;

sentences.zh: 又聞西夏侵掠鄜延，爲腹背患。

translations.literal: it is also heard the Western Xia raid Yan and Yan along the border—a trouble in belly and back.
translations.idiomatic: and the Western Xia raid the frontier—a threat behind as well as before.

sentences.zh: 今莫若移檄蜀帥及川峽四路，共資關中守禦之備，合秦、蜀以衛王室。」

translations.literal: Now it is best to shift proclamation to the Shu commander and the four circuits of Chuan and Xia jointly to supply Guanzhong defense, joining Qin and Shu to guard the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: Summon Shu and the four Chuan circuits to supply Guanzhong and join Qin and Shu in guarding the throne."

sentences.zh: 致虛銳于出師，由澠池屯千秋鎮，爲金將所敗，軍皆潰，退保潼關，而五路之力益耗矣。

translations.literal: Zhixu was keen to march; he encamped at Qianqiu post from Mianchi and was defeated by a Jin general; the army all fled; he retreated to guard Tong Pass—and the five circuits' strength was further wasted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu marched eagerly, was defeated at Qianqiu, fled to Tong Pass, and wasted the five circuits' strength.

sentences.zh: 重募人間道走京城歸報。

translations.literal: Chong recruited men by secret route to run to the capital and report.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent men by secret paths to report to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二帝既北行，重即移檄川、秦十路帥臣，各備禮物往軍前迎奉。

translations.literal: After the two emperors went north, Chong immediately shifted proclamation to the ten circuit commanders of Chuan and Qin, each to prepare gifts and go before the army to welcome and attend.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperors were taken north, he urged the ten Chuan and Qin commanders to prepare to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，高宗即位，重上疏論今急務有四，大患有五。

translations.literal: Before long Gaozong ascended; Chong memorialized on the four urgent tasks of the day and five great ills.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong rose, Chong memorialized four urgent tasks and five great ills.

sentences.zh: 所謂急務者，以車駕西幸爲先，次則建藩鎮、封宗子，通夏國之好，繼青唐之後，使相犄角，以緩敵勢。

translations.literal: The urgent tasks: first the imperial carriage should travel west; next establish frontier towns and enfeoff clansmen; befriend the Western Xia; follow Qingtang—make them horn and hoof to slow the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent tasks: move the court west, enfeoff princes, befriend the Xia, recover allies—to check the enemy.

sentences.zh: 所謂大患者，法令滋彰，朝綱委靡，軍政敗壞，國用竭，民心離。

translations.literal: The great ills: laws increase, court discipline slackens, military affairs fail, state funds are exhausted, people's hearts depart.
translations.idiomatic: Great ills: proliferating laws, slack discipline, broken armies, empty treasury, lost hearts.

sentences.zh: 欲救此者，宜守祖宗成憲，登用忠直，大正賞刑，誠今日之急務。

translations.literal: To save this one should guard the ancestors' established statutes, employ the loyal and upright, and greatly rectify rewards and punishments—that is the urgent task of today.
translations.idiomatic: Remedy: uphold ancestral law, employ the loyal, and rectify reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 長安謀帥，劉岑自河東使還，上亦詢可守關中者，岑以重對，乃以天章閣直學士知京兆府，尋兼京兆府路經略制置使。

translations.literal: Chang'an sought a commander; Liu Cen returned from envoy to Hedong; the emperor also asked who could guard Guanzhong; Cen answered with Chong; he was made Direct Academician of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns and prefect of Jingzhao, soon also Jingzhao circuit pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an needed a defender, Liu Cen named Chong; he became Jingzhao prefect and pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 重前在同州，凡三疏上大元帥府，乞早臨關中以符衆望。

translations.literal: Before this at Tong Prefecture Chong three times memorialized the grand marshal's office begging early arrival in Guanzhong to match the people's hope.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongzhou he had thrice begged the grand marshal to enter Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 且畫三策：一謂鎮撫關中以固根本，然後營屯于漢中，開國于西蜀，此爲策之上；

translations.literal: He also drew three plans: first pacify Guanzhong to fix the root, then camp at Hanzhong and establish the state in western Shu—this is the upper plan;
translations.idiomatic: He offered three plans: secure Guanzhong, then Hanzhong and a Shu base—the best plan;

sentences.zh: 若駐節南陽，控楚、吳、越、齊、趙、魏之師，以臨秦、晉之墟，視敵強弱爲進退，選宗親賢明者開府于關中，此爲策之次；

translations.literal: if the imperial seat is at Nanyang, controlling Chu, Wu, Yue, Qi, Zhao, and Wei troops to face the Qin and Jin ruins, advancing or retreating as the enemy's strength—select a clansman of talent to open a headquarters in Guanzhong—this is the middle plan;
translations.idiomatic: hold Nanyang and rally the southeast—the middle plan;

sentences.zh: 儻因都城，再治城池汴、洛之境，據成皋、崤函之險，悉嚴防守，此策之下；

translations.literal: if one clings to the capital and again repairs Bian and Luo, holding the hazards of Chenggao and Xiaohan, strictly defending—this is the lower plan;
translations.idiomatic: cling to Bian and Luo and fortify—the worst defensible plan;

sentences.zh: 若引兵南度，則國勢微弱，人心離散，此最無策。

translations.literal: if troops are led south across the river, national strength is weak and hearts scatter—this is the plan without plan.
translations.idiomatic: march south across the river—no plan at all.

sentences.zh: 暨至永興，又六上疏，皆以車駕幸關中爲請。

translations.literal: When he reached Yongxing he again six times memorialized, all begging the imperial carriage to favor Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongxing he six times begged the court to enter Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 並條奏關中防河事宜，大意謂：虢、陝殘破，解州、河中已陷，同、華州沿河與金人對壘，邊面亙六百餘里。

translations.literal: He also listed Guanzhong river defense matters in summary: Guo and Shan are ravaged, Jie and Hezhong fallen, Tong and Hua along the river face the Jin—more than six hundred li of frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He detailed the frontier: six hundred li facing the Jin with almost no troops.

sentences.zh: 本路無可戰之兵，乞增以五路兵馬十萬以上，委漕臣儲偫以守關中。

translations.literal: This circuit has no troops fit to fight; I beg add more than one hundred thousand from the five circuits; entrust the transport commissioner to store provisions to hold Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He begged an additional hundred thousand troops and stored grain to hold Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 章凡七八上，朝廷未有所處。

translations.literal: Memorials seven or eight times—the court did nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight memorials went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 重復上疏曰：「關中百二之勢，控制陝西六路，捍蔽川峽四路。

translations.literal: Chong again memorialized: "Guanzhong's strategic hundred-and-two strength controls the six circuits of Shaanxi and shields the four circuits of Chuan and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Guanzhong commands Shaanxi and shields Shu.

sentences.zh: 今蒲、解失守，與敵爲鄰，關中固，則可保秦、蜀十路無虞。

translations.literal: Now Pu and Jie are lost, neighboring the enemy; if Guanzhong is firm, the ten circuits of Qin and Shu can be without worry.
translations.idiomatic: If Guanzhong holds, Qin and Shu are safe.

sentences.zh: 緣逐路帥守、監司各有占護，不相通融。

translations.literal: Formerly each circuit's commanders and transport commissioners each guarded their own and did not coordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders would not coordinate.

sentences.zh: 昨范致虛會合勤王之師，非不竭力，而將帥各自爲謀，不聽節制。

translations.literal: When Fan Zhixu gathered troops to aid the king it was not without effort, yet generals each schemed alone and would not heed command.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu's relief armies fought without unified command.

sentences.zh: 乞選宗親賢明者充京兆牧，或置元帥府，令總管秦、蜀十道兵馬以便宜從事，應帥守、監司並聽節制。

translations.literal: I beg select a clansman of talent as Jingzhao governor, or set a marshal's headquarters to command the ten circuits' troops of Qin and Shu with discretionary power; commanders and transport commissioners all under command.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a prince or marshal to command all ten circuits.

sentences.zh: 緩急則合諸道之兵以衛社稷，不惟可以禦敵，亦可以救郡縣瓦解之失。」

translations.literal: In urgency combine the circuits' troops to guard the altars—not only to resist the enemy but to save the loss of counties and prefectures dissolving."
translations.idiomatic: Only unified command can save the realm and the counties falling away."

sentences.zh: 又乞節制五路兵，俱不報。

translations.literal: He also begged to command the five circuits' troops—all unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to command five circuits—silence again.

sentences.zh: 金將婁宿渡河陷韓城縣，時京兆餘兵皆爲經制使錢蓋調赴行在。

translations.literal: The Jin general Lou crossed the river and took Hancheng County; at that time Jingzhao's remaining troops were all transferred by Commissioner Qian Gai to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: When Lou crossed the river and took Hancheng, Jingzhao's troops had been stripped for the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 重度勢不可支，以書別其父克臣曰：「忠孝不兩立，義不苟生以辱吾父。」

translations.literal: Chong judged the situation could not be sustained and wrote his father Keqin separately: "Loyalty and filial piety cannot both stand; righteousness does not allow living in shame to disgrace my father."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his father: "Loyalty and filial piety cannot both be served—I will not live to shame you."

sentences.zh: 克臣報之曰：「汝能以身徇國，吾含笑入地矣。」

translations.literal: Keqin replied: "You can give body for the state; I will enter the earth with a smile."
translations.idiomatic: His father replied: "Die for the state; I will smile in my grave."

sentences.zh: 及金人入境，重遺書轉運使李唐孺曰：「重平生忠義，不敢辭難。

translations.literal: When the Jin entered the border, Chong sent a letter to Transport Commissioner Li Tangru saying: "Chong's lifelong loyalty dares not shun difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: He told Li Tangru: "I have been loyal all my life and will not shrink from death.

sentences.zh: 始意迎車駕入關，居建瓴之勢，庶可以臨東方。

translations.literal: At first I meant to welcome the imperial carriage into Guanzhong, dwelling in a commanding position, perhaps to face the east; now the carriage has gone south and Guan and Shan have no heavy troops—though I exhaust wit and strength what can be done;
