translations.idiomatic: I hoped to bring the court to Guanzhong; now it has gone south and I have no troops—

sentences.zh: 今車駕南幸矣，關陝又無重兵，雖竭智力何所施，一死報上不足惜。」

translations.literal: Now the carriage has gone south and Guan and Shan have no heavy troops—though I exhaust wit and strength what can be done; one death to answer the ruler is not to be regretted."
translations.idiomatic: The court has gone south and I have no troops—only death remains to serve the throne."

sentences.zh: 及金兵圍城，城中兵不滿千，固守逾旬，外援不至。

translations.literal: When Jin troops besieged the city, troops in the city were fewer than a thousand; they held more than ten days; outside aid did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin besieged the city he had fewer than a thousand men and held ten days without aid.

sentences.zh: 而經制副使傅亮以精銳數百奪門出降，城陷，重以親兵百人血戰。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Fu Liang led several hundred elite troops to seize the gate and surrender; the city fell; Chong with his personal guard of one hundred fought in blood.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang opened the gates with elite troops; the city fell; Chong fought on with a hundred guards.

sentences.zh: 諸將扶重去，重曰：「死吾職也。」

translations.literal: The generals supported Chong to leave; Chong said: "To die is my office."
translations.idiomatic: His officers tried to pull him away; he said: "Death is my duty."

sentences.zh: 戰不已，衆潰，重中流矢死。

translations.literal: Fighting did not cease; the crowd scattered; Chong was struck by a flying arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought until the line broke; a stray arrow killed him.

sentences.zh: 初，唐孺以其書聞，俄以死節報。

translations.literal: At first Tangru reported his letter; soon came report of death in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tangru had reported his letter; soon came word of his death.

sentences.zh: 上哀悼之，贈資政殿學士，後諡恭湣。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him and posthumously enfeoffed him as academician of the Zizheng Hall; later posthumous title Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, posthumously made him Zizheng academician, later posthumous name Reverent and Sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 郭忠孝

translations.literal: Guo Zhongxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhongxiao.

sentences.zh: 郭忠孝，字立之，河南人，簽書樞密院事逵之子。

translations.literal: Guo Zhongxiao, style name Lizhi, was a man of Henan, son of the Deputy Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhongxiao, styled Lizhi, of Henan, was son of Deputy Director of Military Affairs Guo Kui.

sentences.zh: 受《易》、《中庸》于程頤。

translations.literal: He received the Changes and the Doctrine of the Mean from Cheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Changes and the Doctrine of the Mean under Cheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 少以父任補右班殿直，遷右侍禁。

translations.literal: In youth by his father's position he was supplemented as Right Guard Attendant, moved to Right Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father he entered as a Right Guard Attendant.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，換文資，授將作監主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, changed to civil status, and was appointed Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi, took civil rank, and became chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 年逾三十，不忍去親側，多仕于河南筦庫間。

translations.literal: Past thirty he could not bear to leave his parents' side and mostly served in Henan granary posts.
translations.idiomatic: After thirty he stayed near his parents, serving in Henan granary posts.

sentences.zh: 宣和間，爲河東路提舉。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe period he was Hedong transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe he was Hedong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 解梁、猗氏與河東接壤，盜販鹽者數百爲群，歲起大獄，轉相告引，抵罪者衆。

translations.literal: Jie and Yishi bordered Hedong; salt smugglers in hundreds formed bands; each year great cases arose, with mutual accusation—many were punished.
translations.idiomatic: On the Hedong border hundreds smuggled salt; yearly prosecutions ensnared many.

sentences.zh: 忠孝止治其首，餘悉寬貸。

translations.literal: Zhongxiao only punished the leaders; the rest were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiao punished only ringleaders and pardoned the rest.

sentences.zh: 宰相王黼怒之，坐廢格鹽法免。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Wang Fu was angry and dismissed him for violating the salt law.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu removed him for violating the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，召爲軍器少監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang he was summoned as Vice Director of the Armory.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingkang's opening he was summoned as Vice Director of the Armory.

sentences.zh: 入對，以和議爲非是，力陳追擊之策，謂：「兵家忌深入，金人自燕薊興兵，逾河朔，犯都城，其鋒不可當，今銳氣且衰，又顧子女玉帛之獲，故議和以款我師。

translations.literal: On audience he said peace talks were wrong and strongly set forth pursuit: "Armies fear deep penetration—the Jin from Yan and Ji crossed the Hebei and attacked the capital; their edge could not be met; now their sharpness wanes and they also care for women and jade gained—thus they discuss peace to detain our army.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced peace and urged pursuit: "The Jin are spent and greedy—peace is a ruse to hold our armies.

sentences.zh: 今諸道之師集矣，宜乘其惰擊之，若不能擊其歸，他日安能禦其來。」

translations.literal: Now troops of all circuits are gathered—one should strike their slackness; if their return cannot be struck, how later can their coming be resisted?"
translations.idiomatic: Our armies are gathered—strike them now or never hold them off again."

sentences.zh: 上命與宰相吳敏、樞密李綱議，忠孝復條上戰守利害、士馬分合之策十餘事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered discussion with Chief Minister Wu Min and Military Affairs Director Li Gang; Zhongxiao again listed more than ten items of war-and-defense harm and benefit and horse-and-troop division and combination.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to debate with Wu Min and Li Gang, he submitted a dozen plans of war and defense.

sentences.zh: 主和者衆，卒不用其策。

translations.literal: The peace party was numerous; in the end his plan was not used.
translations.idiomatic: The peace faction prevailed; his plans were rejected.

sentences.zh: 改永興軍路提點刑獄，措置保甲。

translations.literal: He was changed to judicial commissioner of Yongxing circuit and arranged the militia.
translations.idiomatic: He became Yongxing judicial commissioner and organized the militia.

sentences.zh: 初，議者請擇保甲十萬刺爲義勇，分隸河朔諸郡。

translations.literal: At first deliberators asked to choose one hundred thousand militia to be drilled as righteous braves, assigned to Hebei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed drilling a hundred thousand militia for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 忠孝曰：「保甲歲久，死亡者衆，擇三萬人守都城可也，河朔騎兵之地，非保甲所宜。」

translations.literal: Zhongxiao said: "The militia for long years—many dead; choose thirty thousand to guard the capital—that suffices; Hebei is land of cavalry—not fit for militia."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiao said: "Thirty thousand for the capital suffice; Hebei needs cavalry, not militia."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: "the cited text..
translations.idiomatic: "the cited text..

sentences.zh: 忠孝亟走關陝，得勝兵三萬，分隸十將，擇一將統之。

translations.literal: Zhongxiao hastened to Guan and Shan and got thirty thousand victorious troops, assigned to ten commanders, one commander to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to Guan-Shan, raised thirty thousand veterans, and organized them under ten commanders.

sentences.zh: 繼遣兵趨澤、潞，聽宣撫司節制。

translations.literal: He then sent troops toward Ze and Lu under pacification command.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent troops toward Ze and Lu under the pacification command.

sentences.zh: 金人再犯京師，永興帥範致虛率諸軍繇淆、澠入援，忠孝曰「金人深入，而河東無守備，願分兵走太行，扼其歸路，彼必來戰，城下之圍可緩。」

translations.literal: When the Jin again attacked the capital, Yongxing commander Fan Zhixu led all armies through Xiao and Mian to aid; Zhongxiao said: "The Jin have penetrated deep while Hedong has no defense—I wish to divide troops along the Taihang to block their return; they must come fight and the siege below the walls can be eased."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked the capital again, Fan Zhixu marched through Xiao and Mian to relieve it; Guo Zhongxiao urged him to detach troops along the Taihang to cut the enemy's retreat and ease the siege.

sentences.zh: 致虛以爲然。

translations.literal: Zhixu thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu agreed.

sentences.zh: 檄河中守席益、馮翊守唐重與忠孝同出河東，爲牽制之舉，大軍盡出函穀。

translations.literal: He shifted orders to Hezhong prefect Xi Yi, Fengxiang prefect Tang Chong, and Zhongxiao together to leave Hedong as a diversion; the main army all left through Hangu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Orders went to Xi Yi, Tang Chong, and Zhongxiao to raid Hedong while the main army marched out through Hangu Pass.

sentences.zh: 忠孝獨以蒲、解軍三千至猗氏，遇金人，破之。

translations.literal: Zhongxiao alone with three thousand Pu and Jie troops reached Yishi, met the Jin, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiao alone with three thousand men reached Yishi and routed the Jin.

sentences.zh: 逾絳州，破太平砦，斬首數百級。

translations.literal: Crossing Jiang Prefecture he took Taiping Fortress and beheaded several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed into Jiangzhou, took Taiping Fortress, and slew hundreds.

sentences.zh: 攻平陽，入其郛。

translations.literal: He attacked Pingyang and entered the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Pingyang and entered its outer city.

sentences.zh: 會大軍失利淆、澠間，乃引還。

translations.literal: As the main army was defeated between Xiao and Mian he led back.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army was defeated at Xiao-Mian he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及金人犯永興，兵寡，或勸忠孝以監司出巡，可以避禍。

translations.literal: When the Jin attacked Yongxing, troops were few; some urged Zhongxiao as commissioner to go on inspection to avoid calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin besieged Yongxing, some urged him to leave on inspection to escape.

sentences.zh: 忠孝不答，與經略唐重分城而守。

translations.literal: Zhongxiao did not answer and with Commissioner Tang Chong divided the city to defend.
translations.idiomatic: He refused and split the defense with Tang Chong.

sentences.zh: 忠孝主西壁，唐重主東壁。

translations.literal: Zhongxiao held the west wall; Tang Chong held the east wall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiao held the west wall; Chong the east.

sentences.zh: 金人陳城下，忠孝募人以神臂弓射之，敵不得前。

translations.literal: The Jin arrayed below the city; Zhongxiao recruited men to shoot with divine-bow crossbows; the enemy could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He used divine-bow crossbowmen to keep the Jin from the walls.

sentences.zh: 已而攻陷城東南隅，忠孝與重及副總管楊宗閔、轉運副使桑景詢、判官曾謂、經略主管機宜文字王尚、提舉軍馬武功大夫程迪俱死之。

translations.literal: Soon they attacked and took the southeast corner of the city; Zhongxiao with Chong and Vice Commander Yang Zongmin, Vice Transport Commissioner Sang Jingxun, Administrator Zeng Wei, planning officer Wang Shang, and martial-officer Commissioner Cheng Di all died.
translations.idiomatic: When the southeast corner fell, Zhongxiao, Chong, Yang Zongmin, Sang Jingxun, Zeng Wei, Wang Shang, and Cheng Di died fighting.

sentences.zh: 朝廷贈忠孝大中大夫。

translations.literal: The court posthumously enfeoffed Zhongxiao as Grandee of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made Zhongxiao Grandee of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 子雍，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Yong has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 程迪，字惠老，開封人。

translations.literal: Cheng Di.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Di.

sentences.zh: 父博古，部鄜延兵戰死永樂。

translations.literal: Cheng Di, style name Huilao, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Di, styled Huilao, was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 迪以門蔭得官。

translations.literal: His father Bogu died in battle at Yongle leading troops of Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bogu died at Yongle leading Fuyan troops.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，從楊惟中征方臘有功，加武功大夫、榮州團練使、瀘南潼川府路走馬承受公事。

translations.literal: Di gained office by yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Di entered service through yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 諸使合薦迪忠義謀略，可任將帥，召赴行在。

translations.literal: In Xuanhe he followed Yang Weizhong against Fang La with merit, was added Martial Officer, Regimental Trainer of Rongzhou, and courier commissioner of Luzhou and Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe he campaigned against Fang La, won merit, and rose to martial officer and Luzhou courier commissioner.

sentences.zh: 經略制置使唐重以敵迫近，留迪提舉軍馬，措置民兵以爲備。

translations.literal: Several commissioners jointly recommended Di's loyal stratagem fit to command troops; he was summoned to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners recommended his loyalty and strategy; he was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 金人已自同州渡河，或勸迪還蜀，迪思有以報國，不從。

translations.literal: Commissioner Tang Chong, as the enemy pressed near, kept Di to direct troops and arrange militia as preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Chong kept him to direct troops and train militia as the enemy neared.

sentences.zh: 乃詣種氏諸豪，謀率衆保險，俟其勢稍衰，出奇擊之。

translations.literal: The Jin had already crossed from Tong Prefecture; some urged Di to return to Shu; Di thought to answer the state and would not.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged flight to Shu; Di chose to stay and serve.

sentences.zh: 轉運使桑景詢知其謀，以告唐重，揭榜許民擇險自固。

translations.literal: He then went to the Zhong clan magnates, plotting to lead the masses to hold the passes and wait until their strength slackened, then strike with a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied local magnates to hold the passes and strike when the Jin weakened.

sentences.zh: 會前河東經制使傅亮建議當守不當避，重從之，以亮爲制置副使，去者悉還。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Sang Jingxun knew his plan and reported to Tang Chong; a placard allowed the people to choose passes and secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Jingxun reported his plan; Chong posted notices allowing people to flee to the hills.

sentences.zh: 既而金兵益迫，重乃以迪提舉永興路軍馬，措置民兵，令迪行視南山諸穀，將運金帛徙治其中。

translations.literal: Former Hedong Commissioner Fu Liang argued one should defend and not flee; Chong followed this, made Liang vice commissioner; those who had left all returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang argued for holding the city; Chong made him vice commissioner and recalled fugitives.

sentences.zh: 因召土豪，集民兵以補軍籍。

translations.literal: Soon the Jin pressed harder; Chong then made Di direct Yongxing troops and militia, ordering Di to survey southern mountain valleys and move gold and silk to govern within them.
translations.idiomatic: As pressure grew, Chong sent Di to survey southern valleys for relocating stores.

sentences.zh: 會應募者衆，亮語重曰：「人心如此，假以旬日，守備且具，奈何望風棄去。」

translations.literal: He also summoned local magnates and gathered militia to fill the army rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned magnates and enrolled militia.

sentences.zh: 重大然之，即檄諸司聽亮節制。

translations.literal: When many volunteered, Liang said to Chong: "Hearts are thus—in ten days defenses will be ready—why flee at rumor?"
translations.idiomatic: When volunteers poured in, Liang said: "Morale is high—in ten days we are ready; why flee?"

sentences.zh: 金人近城，迪又欲選兵迎戰，使老稚得趣險，尚可以活十萬人。

translations.literal: Chong greatly approved and shifted all offices to heed Liang's command.
translations.idiomatic: Chong agreed and put Liang in command.

sentences.zh: 亮執議城守，金人四面急攻，外無援兵，迪率諸司及統制偏裨以下東鄉會盟：「危急必以死相應，誓不與敵俱生。」

translations.literal: When the Jin neared the city, Di again wished to choose troops to meet them so old and young could hurry to safety—perhaps one hundred thousand could live.
translations.idiomatic: Di wanted a sortie so civilians could reach the hills—perhaps saving a hundred thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 慷慨嗚咽，同盟皆感泣。

translations.literal: Liang held to defending the city; the Jin attacked fiercely on four sides; there was no relief; Di led all commissioners and commanders below colonel eastward to ally in oath: "In extremity we must answer with death, swearing not to live with the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Liang insisted on static defense; Di led the officers in an oath to die rather than yield.

sentences.zh: 城破，乃自亮所分地始。

translations.literal: They wept in grief; all who allied were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: They wept; all who swore were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 亮先出降，衆潰。

translations.literal: When the city fell, it began from Liang's sector.
translations.idiomatic: The breach began where Liang had commanded.

sentences.zh: 迪率其徒行徇于衆曰：「敵仇我矣，降亦死，戰亦死！」

translations.literal: Liang first went out to surrender; the masses scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Liang surrendered first; the line collapsed.

sentences.zh: 努力與鬥，憤怒大呼，口流血，士皆感奮，多所斬殺。

translations.literal: Di led his followers through the crowd crying: "The enemy hates us—surrender is death, fight is death!"
translations.idiomatic: Di marched his men shouting: "Surrender or fight—both mean death—so fight!"

sentences.zh: 迪冒飛矢，持短兵接戰數十合，身被創幾遍，絕而復蘇，猶厲聲叱戰不已，遂死之。

translations.literal: They strove in battle; angrily he shouted; blood flowed from his mouth; soldiers were all stirred and killed many.
translations.idiomatic: They fought fiercely; he shouted until blood ran from his mouth; his men slew many Jin.

sentences.zh: 麾下士舁置空室中，比屋皆燼，室獨不火，及斂，容色如生。

translations.literal: Di braved flying arrows, fought hand-to-hand for several tens of bouts, was wounded throughout, fainted and revived, still fiercely shouted battle without cease, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought hand-to-hand through many wounds, fainted and rose again, and died still shouting.

sentences.zh: 詔贈明州觀察使，諡恭湣。

translations.literal: His subordinates placed him in an empty room; neighboring houses were all ash; that room alone did not burn; when gathered for burial his face was as in life.
translations.idiomatic: His body lay in a room untouched while the city burned; in burial his face looked alive.

sentences.zh: 子昌諤。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as observer of Mingzhou; posthumous title Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him observer of Mingzhou, posthumous name Reverent and Sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 徐徽言

translations.literal: His son Chang'e.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chang'e.

sentences.zh: 徐徽言，字彥猷，衢之西安人。

translations.literal: Xu Huiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huiyan.

sentences.zh: 少爲諸生，泛涉書傳。

translations.literal: Xu Huiyan, style name Yanyou, was a native of Xi'an in Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huiyan, styled Yanyou, was from Xi'an in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 負氣豪舉，有奇志，喜談功名事。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student, broadly reading books and records.
translations.idiomatic: As a student he read widely.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，詔求材武士，韓忠彥、范純粹、劉仲武以徽言應詔，召見崇德殿，賜武舉絕倫及第。

translations.literal: He bore a bold, heroic spirit, had a strange ambition, and delighted in discussing merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and ambitious, he loved talk of service and fame.

sentences.zh: 曆保德軍監押，以邊功加閣門祗候、平陽府軍馬鈴轄，權知保德軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan an edict sought martial talent; Han Zhongyan, Fan Chunzhi, and Liu Zhongwu presented Huiyan; he was summoned to the Chongde Hall and granted martial examination supreme and first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan's second year he was presented as martial talent, examined at Chongde Hall, and topped the military examination.

sentences.zh: 改總領河西軍馬，以討西夏功，累遷秉義郎。

translations.literal: He served as Baode Army controller, was added Palace Gate Attendant and Pingyang military controller, and acting prefect of Baode Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the Baode frontier, became palace gate attendant and Pingyang military controller, and acted as Baode prefect.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，將伐燕，命太原帥張孝純招河西帳族，遣徽言入其地。

translations.literal: He was changed to overall commander of Hexi troops; for campaigning against the Western Xia he was repeatedly promoted to Integrity Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Made overall Hexi commander, he won repeated promotions fighting the Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 帳族拒而射之，徽言迎戰破之，遂定天德、雲內兩城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuanhe, about to attack Yan, the court ordered Taiyuan commander Zhang Xiaochun to recruit Hexi tribal forces; Huiyan was sent into their lands.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe's fourth year, ordered into tribal lands to recruit allies for the Yan campaign.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使童貫嫉其功，檄太原不得違節度。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuanhe, about to attack Yan, the court ordered Taiyuan commander Zhang Xiaochun to recruit Hexi tribal forces; Huiyan was sent into their lands.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe's fourth year, ordered into tribal lands to recruit allies for the Yan campaign.

sentences.zh: 復棄去。

translations.literal: The tribes resisted and shot; Huiyan met them in battle and defeated them, then secured Tiande and Yunnei cities.
translations.idiomatic: When tribes resisted, he defeated them and secured Tiande and Yunnei.

sentences.zh: 孝純先定朔、武二州，亦不能守。

translations.literal: the cited text..
translations.idiomatic: the cited text..

sentences.zh: 改知火山軍兼統制河西軍馬，徙赴石州。

translations.literal: He again abandoned them.
translations.idiomatic: He was forced to abandon his gains.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，遷武翼郎、閣門宣贊舍人。

translations.literal: Xiaochun had first taken Shuo and Wu prefectures yet also could not hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaochun had taken Shuo and Wu but could not hold them either.

sentences.zh: 金人圍太原，分兵絕饟道，自隰、石以北，命令不通者累月。

translations.literal: He was changed to govern Volcano Army while overall commanding Hexi troops, then sent to Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Volcano Army, commanded Hexi troops, then went to Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 徽言以三十人渡河，一戰破之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang he was moved to Martial Wings Gentleman and Palace Proclamation Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingkang's opening he became Martial Wings Gentleman and palace proclamation attendant.

sentences.zh: 遷武經郎、知晉寧軍兼嵐石路沿邊安撫使。

translations.literal: The Jin besieged Taiyuan and divided troops to cut grain routes; from Xi and Shi northward orders did not pass for many months.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin besieged Taiyuan and cut supply lines; north of Xi and Shi no orders passed for months.

sentences.zh: 金人再犯京師，陝西制置使範致虛糾合五路兵赴難，檄徽言守河西。

translations.literal: Huiyan with thirty men crossed the river and broke them in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: With thirty men he crossed the river and broke the blockade in one fight.

sentences.zh: 欽宗割兩河以紓禍，同知樞密院事聶昌出河東，爲金人所劫，以便宜割河西三州隸西夏。

translations.literal: He was moved to Martial Classic Gentleman and prefect of Jinning Army while frontier comfort commissioner of Lan and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted, he became Jinning prefect and frontier comfort commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉寧軍民大恐，曰：「棄麟、府、豐，晉寧豈能獨存！」

translations.literal: When the Jin again attacked the capital, Shaanxi Commissioner Fan Zhixu gathered five circuits' troops to aid; he shifted Huiyan to guard Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was attacked again, Fan Zhixu summoned aid; Huiyan was left to guard Hexi.

sentences.zh: 徽言曰：「此使人矯詔耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong ceded the two He to ease calamity; Vice Director of Military Affairs Nie Chang went to Hedong, was seized by the Jin, and by convenience ceded three Hexi prefectures to the Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzong ceded the Two He; Nie Chang was seized and the Jin ceded three Hexi prefectures to the Xia.

sentences.zh: 三郡在河西，設有詔，猶當執奏，況無之耶！」

translations.literal: The people of Jinning Army were greatly afraid, saying: "If Lin, Fu, and Feng are abandoned, how can Jinning alone remain!"
translations.idiomatic: Jinning panicked: "If Lin, Fu, and Feng are lost, we cannot stand alone!"

sentences.zh: 遂率兵復取三州，夏人所置守長皆出降，徽言慰遣之。

translations.literal: Huiyan said: "This is the envoy's forged edict."
translations.idiomatic: Huiyan said: "This is a forged edict."

sentences.zh: 又並取嵐、石凳州，教戈舡卒乘羊皮渾脫亂流以掩敵。

translations.literal: The three prefectures are in Hexi—even if there were an edict one should still memorialize; how much less when there is none!"
translations.idiomatic: "Even a real edict would need memorial—even more when there is none!"

sentences.zh: 金人益備克胡砦、吳堡津，遣守領爲九州都統，與晉寧對壘。

translations.literal: He then led troops and recovered the three prefectures; Xia-appointed prefects all came out to surrender; Huiyan comforted and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He marched, recovered the three prefectures, and sent Xia officials home.

sentences.zh: 徽言出奇兵襲逐之。

translations.literal: He also together took Lan, Shi, and Deng prefectures, teaching boat soldiers to ride sheepskin rafts in turbulent current to surprise the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Lan, Shi, and Deng, using sheepskin rafts for river raids.

sentences.zh: 時河東郡縣淪沒，遺民日徯王師之至。

translations.literal: The Jin further prepared Kehu Fortress and Wubao Ford, sent a commander as nine-prefecture commander-in-chief, and faced Jinning in camp.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin fortified crossings and camped against Jinning.

sentences.zh: 徽言陰結汾、晉土豪數十萬，約復故地則奏官爲守長，聽世襲。

translations.literal: Huiyan sent surprise troops to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: He drove them off with surprise attacks.

sentences.zh: 條其事以聞，俟報可，即身率精甲搗太原，徑取雁門，留兵戍守；

translations.literal: At that time Hedong prefectures and counties were lost; surviving people daily awaited the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: As Hedong fell, refugees daily awaited the Song armies.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「定全晉則形勝爲我有，中原當指期克復，投機一時，會不可失。」

translations.literal: Huiyan secretly joined several hundred thousand strongmen of Fen and Jin, agreeing that if old territory was recovered they would be memorialized as hereditary prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly rallied hundreds of thousands in Fen and Jin, promising hereditary office if they recovered the land.

sentences.zh: 奏上，詔徽言聽王庶節制，議遂格。

translations.literal: He listed the matter to report; awaiting approval he personally led elite armor to strike Taiyuan, straight to take Yanmen, leaving troops to garrison;
translations.idiomatic: He reported the plan and, awaiting approval, prepared to strike Taiyuan and Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 金人忌徽言，欲速拔晉寧以除患。

translations.literal: and said: "Secure all Jin and the strategic advantage is ours; the central plain can be recovered on schedule—seize the moment; the meeting cannot be lost."
translations.idiomatic: "Hold all Jin and the heartland can be retaken—this chance must not be lost."

sentences.zh: 建炎二年冬，自蒲津涉河圍之。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, an edict made Huiyan heed Wang Shu's command; deliberation was again blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The court put him under Wang Shu; the plan was blocked.

sentences.zh: 先是徽言移府州，約折可求夾攻金人。

translations.literal: The Jin feared Huiyan and wished quickly to take Jinning to remove the trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin feared him and hurried to take Jinning.

sentences.zh: 可求降，金將婁宿挾至城下以招徽言。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Jianyan they crossed at Pu Ford and besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan's second winter they crossed at Pu Ford and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 徽言故與可求爲姻，乃登陴以大義噍數之。

translations.literal: Before this Huiyan had moved to Fuzhou, agreeing with Zhe Keshou to attack the Jin jointly.
translations.idiomatic: He had moved to Fuzhou, planning a joint attack with Zhe Keshou.

sentences.zh: 可求仰曰：「君于我胡大無情？」

translations.literal: Keshou surrendered; Jin general Lou brought him below the wall to summon Huiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Keshou surrendered; Lou brought him to the walls to summon Huiyan.

sentences.zh: 徽言攝弓厲言曰：「爾于國家不有情，我尚于爾何情？

translations.literal: Huiyan had been related to Keshou by marriage; he ascended the wall and with great righteousness reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: Once related by marriage, Huiyan denounced Keshou from the wall.

sentences.zh: 寧惟我無情，此矢尤無情。」

translations.literal: Keshou looked up: "Why are you so without feeling toward me?"
translations.idiomatic: Keshou cried: "Why are you so cruel to me?"

sentences.zh: 一發中之，可求走，因出兵縱擊，遂斬婁宿孛堇之子。

translations.literal: Huiyan drew his bow and said fiercely: "You were without feeling toward the state—why should I have feeling toward you?"
translations.idiomatic: Huiyan drew his bow: "You betrayed the state—why should I spare you?"

sentences.zh: 當是時，環河東皆已陷，獨晉寧屹然孤墉，橫當強敵，勢相百不抗。

translations.literal: Not only am I without feeling—this arrow is also without feeling."
translations.idiomatic: "This arrow has no feeling either."

sentences.zh: 徽言堅壁持久，撫摩疲傷，遣沒人泅河，召民之逃伏山谷者幾萬衆，浮筏西渡，與金人鏖河上，大小數十戰，所俘殺過當。

translations.literal: One shot hit him; Keshou fled; he then led troops out and struck, beheading Lou's son the commander.
translations.idiomatic: He shot Keshou, sallied forth, and slew Lou's son.

sentences.zh: 晉寧號天下險，徽言廣外城，東壓河，下塹不測，譙堞雄固，備械甚整。

translations.literal: At that time all around the river east was lost; only Jinning stood a lone bastion, blocking the strong enemy, strength a hundred to one not matching.
translations.idiomatic: All Hedong had fallen; only Jinning stood alone against overwhelming odds.

sentences.zh: 命諸將畫隅分守，敵至則自致死力，以勁兵往來爲遊援。

translations.literal: Huiyan firmly walled for the long term, comforted the weary and wounded, sent divers across the river, summoned people hiding in mountain valleys—nearly ten thousand—rafted west, and on the river battled the Jin in great and small fights several tens of times, captives and kills exceeding their losses.
translations.idiomatic: He held for months, rescued refugees, fought dozens of river battles, and killed more than he lost.

sentences.zh: 金進攻數敗，不得志，圍之益急。

translations.literal: Jinning was called the world's strongest hazard; Huiyan extended the outer wall, pressed the east upon the river, dug a moat unfathomable, towers and parapets mighty and firm, weapons very complete.
translations.idiomatic: He strengthened Jinning's famed defenses—walls on the river, deep moats, and ample arms.

sentences.zh: 晉甯俗不井飲，寄汲于河。

translations.literal: He ordered the generals each to guard a sector; when the enemy came they gave their utmost; with crack troops coming and going as mobile relief.
translations.idiomatic: Generals held sectors and mobile reserves struck wherever the Jin attacked.

sentences.zh: 金人載茭石湮壅支流，城中水乏絕，儲偫浸罄，鎧仗空敝，人人惴憂，知殞亡無日。

translations.literal: The Jin attacked several times and were defeated, could not achieve their aim; the siege grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated assaults failed; the siege tightened.

sentences.zh: 徽言能得衆心，奮枵餓傷夷之餘，裒折槊斷刃，以死固守。

translations.literal: The custom of Jinning did not draw from wells; they relied on drawing from the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jinning drank from the river, not wells.

sentences.zh: 既自度不支，取炮機、篦格，凡守具悉火之，曰：「無以遺敵。」

translations.literal: The Jin loaded rushes and stones to block tributary streams; water in the city failed and stores were gradually exhausted; armor and weapons were empty and worn; every man feared and knew death was near.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dammed the river; water and stores ran out; arms failed; all knew death was near.

sentences.zh: 遣人間道馳書其兄昌言曰：「徽言孤國恩死矣，兄其勉事君。」

translations.literal: Huiyan could win the people's hearts; with the starving and wounded he gathered broken spears and snapped blades and died defending.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied starving men with broken weapons to die defending.

sentences.zh: 一夕，裨校李位、石贇系帛書飛笴上，陰約婁宿啟外郭納金兵。

translations.literal: Judging he could not sustain, he took catapults and wicker barriers and all defense gear and burned them, saying: "Leave nothing for the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the end was near, he burned the engines and said: "Leave nothing for the enemy."

sentences.zh: 徽言與太原路兵馬都監孫昂決戰門中，所格殺甚衆，退嬰牙城以守。

translations.literal: He sent a man by secret route with a letter to his elder brother Changyan: "Huiyan has alone owed the state's grace and will die; elder brother, strive to serve the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his brother: "I die for the state; serve the emperor well."

sentences.zh: 金人攻之不已，徽言置妻子室中，積薪自焚。

translations.literal: One night, lieutenants Li Wei and Shi Yun tied silk letters on flying bolts, secretly agreeing with Lou to open the outer wall and admit Jin troops.
translations.idiomatic: Officers Li Wei and Shi Yun plotted with Lou to open the gates.

sentences.zh: 仗劍坐堂上，慷慨語將士：「我天子守土臣，義不見蔑敵手。」

translations.literal: Huiyan with Taiyuan military controller Sun Ang fought a decisive battle in the gate; they killed many; retreating they nursed the inner citadel to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyan and Sun Ang fought at the gates, slew many, then held the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 因拔佩刀自擬，左右號救持之急，金兵猥至，挾徽言以去，然猶憚其威名。

translations.literal: The Jin attacked without cease; Huiyan placed wife and children in a room, piled firewood, and burned himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin pressed on; he piled firewood around his family to burn them and himself.

sentences.zh: 婁宿得徽言所親說徽言：「盍具冠ＡＸ見金帥。」

translations.literal: Sword in hand he sat in the hall and spoke generously to the officers: "I am the Son of Heaven's guardian of the soil—by righteousness I will not be seen in the enemy's hands."
translations.idiomatic: Sword in hand he told his officers: "A guardian of the realm does not fall alive into enemy hands."

sentences.zh: 徽言斥曰：「朝章，覲君父禮，以入穹廬可乎？

translations.literal: He drew his belt dagger to stab himself; left and right cried and held him urgently; the Jin crowded in and seized Huiyan away, yet still feared his fierce name.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to stab himself; the Jin seized him alive, still in awe of his name.

sentences.zh: 汝汙偽官，不即愧死，顧以爲榮，且爲敵人搖吻作說客耶？

translations.literal: Lou had Huiyan's close associate persuade him: "Why not prepare cap and hat to see the Jin commander?"
translations.idiomatic: Lou's men urged him to dress and submit.

sentences.zh: 不急去，吾力猶能搏殺汝。」

translations.literal: Lou then went to see Huiyan and said: "The two emperors have gone north—for whom do you hold this?"
translations.idiomatic: Lou asked: "The emperors are gone—for whom do you hold Jinning?"

sentences.zh: 婁宿就見徽言，語曰：「二帝北去，爾其爲誰守此？」

translations.literal: Huiyan said: "I hold for the Jianyan Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "For the Jianyan emperor."

sentences.zh: 徽言曰：「吾爲建炎天子守。」

translations.literal: Lou said: "My troops have already gone south; affairs of the central plain are not yet known—why torment yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Lou said: "Our armies are south—the heartland is uncertain—why suffer?"

sentences.zh: 婁宿曰：「我兵己南矣，中原事未可知，何自苦爲？」

translations.literal: Huiyan angrily said: "I hate that I cannot leave my corpse among you to see the Son of Heaven again; I will repay Emperor Taizu and Taizong underground—how would I know anything else!"
translations.idiomatic: He raged: "I regret only that I cannot kill you all before I join Taizu and Taizong in death!"

sentences.zh: 徽言怒曰：「吾恨不屍汝輩歸見天子，將以死報太祖、太宗地下，庸知其他！」

translations.literal: Lou again produced Jin orders: "If you can bend a little, I will make you hereditary commander of Yan'an for generations and give you all Shaanxi lands together."
translations.idiomatic: Lou offered Yan'an and all Shaanxi if he would submit.

sentences.zh: 婁宿又出金制曰：「能小屈，當使汝世帥延安，舉陝地並有之。」

translations.literal: Huiyan was the more angry and cursed: "I bear the state's thick grace; to die upright is my place—how could these knees bend for you fellows!"
translations.idiomatic: He cursed: "The state favored me—death is my due; these knees will not bend for you!"

sentences.zh: 徽言益怒，罵曰：「吾荷國厚恩，死正吾所，此膝詎爲汝輩屈耶？

translations.literal: You should personally blade me; let no others add blows before my eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Kill me yourself—do not let others touch me.

sentences.zh: 汝當親刃我，不可使餘人見加。」

translations.literal: Lou raised his halberd toward him, hoping to see fear."
translations.idiomatic: Lou raised his halberd, watching for fear."

sentences.zh: 婁宿舉戟向之，覬其懼狀。

translations.literal: Huiyan opened his robe and met the blade; his manner was calm.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyan bared his chest to the blade, calm as ever.

sentences.zh: 徽言披衽迎刃，意象自若。

translations.literal: They gave him wine; he held the cup and threw it at Lou: "Would I still drink your wine?"
translations.idiomatic: Offered wine, he hurled the cup at Lou: "Your wine?"

sentences.zh: 飲以酒，持杯擲婁宿曰：「我尚飲汝酒乎？」

translations.literal: He reviled slowly without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed without stopping.

sentences.zh: 慢罵不已。

translations.literal: The Jin knew he could not be bent and shot him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he would not yield, they shot him.

sentences.zh: 金人知不可屈，遂射殺之。

translations.literal: Nianhan heard of his death and angrily said to Lou: "You are coarse and fierce—why kill a man of righteousness to satisfy your private will?"
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan rebuked Lou for killing a righteous man out of spite.

sentences.zh: 粘罕聞其死，怒婁宿曰：「爾粗狠，何專殺義人以逞爾私？」

translations.literal: He punished him very cruelly.
translations.idiomatic: He punished Lou severely.

sentences.zh: 治其罪甚慘。

translations.literal: At first Huiyan and Liu Guangshi had been friends since boyhood.
translations.idiomatic: He and Liu Guangshi had been friends since youth.

sentences.zh: 初，徽言與劉光世束發雅故。

translations.literal: Guangshi was ordered to aid Taiyuan, stopped at Wubao Ford, and halted without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi was ordered to relieve Taiyuan but halted at Wubao Ford.

sentences.zh: 光世被命援太原，次吳堡津，輒頓不進。

translations.literal: Huiyan shifted letters urging him to march; he did not listen;
translations.idiomatic: Huiyan urged him on; he lingered;

sentences.zh: 徽言移書趣行，未聽；

translations.literal: he again told him Taiyuan's peril could not be held and morning and evening looked for rescue—a commander ordered to urgent aid should not delay and incur the crime of disobedience; Guangshi still advanced and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyan warned that Taiyuan would fall without swift aid; Guangshi still hesitated.

sentences.zh: 又諭以太原危不守，旦暮望救，總管承詔赴急，不宜稽固取方命罪，光世猶前卻。

translations.literal: Huiyan immediately exposed a memorial impeaching his delay, sealed a copy and gave it to him; Guangshi in panic led his route on.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyan memorialized against him and handed him the sealed copy; Guangshi marched in panic.

sentences.zh: 徽言即露章劾其逗撓，封副與之，光世惶遽引道。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun and several commissioners in succession reported death in loyalty; Gaozong struck the table in shock and grief and said to the chief ministers: "Xu Huiyan answered the state and died on the frontier, facing difficulty without bending—loyalty pierced sun and moon—far beyond Yan Zhenqing and Duan Xiushi."
translations.idiomatic: When reports reached Gaozong, he mourned and told his ministers that Huiyan's loyalty surpassed Yan Zhenqing and Duan Xiushi.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使張浚與諸使者相繼以死節事聞，高宗撫幾震悼，顧謂宰相曰：「徐徽言報國死封疆，臨難不屈，忠貫日月，過于顏真卿、段秀實遠矣。

translations.literal: If there is not reward, how can loyalty be encouraged and shown to later generations?
translations.idiomatic: "Without reward, how will we encourage loyalty for ages to come?

sentences.zh: 不有以寵之，何以勸忠，昭示來世。」

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as observer of Jinzhou; posthumous title Zhongzhuang."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made observer of Jinzhou with the name Loyal and Stalwart."

sentences.zh: 乃贈晉州觀察使，諡忠壯。

translations.literal: Again posthumously enfeoffed as military commissioner of Zhanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again made military commissioner of Zhanghua.

sentences.zh: 再贈彰化軍節度。

translations.literal: Sun Ang also drew his blade wishing to stab himself; the Jin crowded him to the army front; he did not yield and died—to this he was posthumously enfeoffed as Loyal Gentleman and regimental trainer.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ang tried to kill himself, was taken alive, and died unbroken—posthumously honored as Loyal Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 孫昂，亦引刀欲自刺，金人擁至軍前，不屈而死，至是贈成忠郎、圍練使。

translations.literal: Huiyan's son Gang had died in the same affair, and his nephew Shi also died defending Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gang died with him; his nephew Shi died defending Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 徽言子岡既同死事，而從孫適亦以守安豐死。

translations.literal: Ang's father Yi, at the end of Xuanhe governed Shuoning Prefecture, rescued Taiyuan, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ang's father Yi had died rescuing Taiyuan under Huizong.

sentences.zh: 昂父翊，宣和末知朔寧府，救太原，死于陣。

translations.literal: Each generation was famed for loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The family was famed for loyalty through generations.

sentences.zh: 各世著忠義雲。

translations.literal: Each generation was famed for loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The family was famed for loyalty through generations.

sentences.zh: 向子韶

translations.literal: Xiang Zishao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Zishao.

sentences.zh: 向子韶，字和卿，開封人，神宗後再從侄也。

translations.literal: Xiang Zishao, style name Heqing, was a man of Kaifeng, a great-grandnephew of Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Zishao, styled Heqing, of Kaifeng, was a great-grandnephew of Emperor Shenzong.

sentences.zh: 年十五入太學，登元符三年進士第。

translations.literal: At fifteen he entered the Imperial College and passed the jinshi in the third year of Yuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial College at fifteen and passed the jinshi in Yuanfu's third year.

sentences.zh: 特恩改承事郎，授荊南府節度判官，累官至京東轉運副使。

translations.literal: By special grace he was changed to Gentleman for Court Service and appointed military judge of Jingnan Prefecture, accumulating to Vice Transport Commissioner of the Eastern Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Jingnan judge to vice transport commissioner of the eastern capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 屬郡郭奉世進萬緡羨餘，戶部聶昌請賞之以勸天下。

translations.literal: The prefect Guo Fengshi presented ten thousand strings of surplus; Household Minister Nie Chang asked to reward this to encourage the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Prefect Guo Fengshi offered surplus revenue, Nie Chang wanted to reward him to encourage others.

sentences.zh: 子韶劾奉世，且言近臣首開聚斂之端，浸不可長，士論韙之。

translations.literal: Zishao impeached Fengshi and said recent ministers had opened the head of accumulation—this must not be lengthened; opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zishao impeached Fengshi, warning that rewarding surplus-taking would spread; opinion praised him.

sentences.zh: 以父憂免，起復，知淮寧府。

translations.literal: He left on father's mourning, was recalled, and governed Huaining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he governed Huaining.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，金人犯淮甯，子韶率諸弟城守，諭士民曰：「汝等墳墓之國，去此何之，吾與汝當死守。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan the Jin attacked Huaining; Zishao led his younger brothers to defend the walls and told soldiers and people: "This is the land of your ancestors' graves—where else would you go? I and you must die defending together."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked Huaining in Jianyan's second year, he told the people: "This is your ancestors' land—we die here together."

sentences.zh: 時有東兵四千人，第三將岳景綬欲棄城率軍民走行在，子韶不從，景綬引兵迎敵而死。

translations.literal: At that time there were four thousand eastern troops; the third commander Yue Jingshou wished to abandon the city and lead soldiers and people to the traveling court; Zishao would not agree; Jingshou led troops to meet the enemy and died.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yue Jingshou wanted to flee; Zishao refused; Jingshou sallied and died.

sentences.zh: 金人晝夜攻城，子韶親擐甲胄，冒矢石，遣其弟子率赴宗澤乞援兵，未至，城陷。

translations.literal: The Jin day and night attacked the city; Zishao personally donned armor, braved arrows and stones, sent his younger brother's son to beg relief of Zong Ze; before it arrived the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in armor, sent a nephew to Zong Ze for aid, and the city fell before help came.

sentences.zh: 子韶率軍民巷戰，力屈爲所執。

translations.literal: Zishao led soldiers and people in lane fighting; strength exhausted he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the alleys until captured.

sentences.zh: 金人坐城上，欲降之，酌酒于前，左右抑令屈膝，子韶直立不動，戟手責駡，金人殺之。

translations.literal: The Jin sat on the wall, wished to make him surrender, poured wine before him; left and right pressed him to bend knees; Zishao stood straight unmoved, pointed and reviled; the Jin killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They offered wine and demanded his knees; he stood, cursed them, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 其弟新知唐州子褒、朝請郎子家等與闔門皆遇害，惟一子鴻六歲得存。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Xin, newly made prefect of Tangzhou Zibao, and Court Gentleman Zijia and the whole household all suffered disaster; only one son Hong, six years old, survived.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers and household perished; only his six-year-old son Hong survived.

sentences.zh: 事聞，再贈通議大夫，官其家六人，後諡忠毅。

translations.literal: When heard, he was again posthumously enfeoffed as Grandee for Court Discussion and six of his household were given office; later posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously honored him, ennobled six kin, and gave the posthumous name Loyal and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 初，金人至淮甯府，楊時聞之曰：「子韶必死矣。」

translations.literal: At first when the Jin reached Huaining Prefecture, Yang Shi heard and said: "Zishao will certainly die."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin came, Yang Shi said: "Zishao will surely die."

sentences.zh: 蓋知其素守者雲。

translations.literal: It was because he knew what he had long upheld.
translations.idiomatic: He knew Zishao's character.

sentences.zh: 楊邦乂

translations.literal: Yang Bangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bangyi.

sentences.zh: 楊邦乂，字晞稷，吉州吉水人。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in past and present, by staff selection he passed the jinshi; meeting troubled times he often pledged himself by integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Learned in history, he passed the jinshi and in troubled times held himself to integrity.

sentences.zh: 博通古今，以舍選登進士第，遭時多艱，每以節義自許。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in past and present, by staff selection he passed the jinshi; meeting troubled times he often pledged himself by integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Learned in history, he passed the jinshi and in troubled times held himself to integrity.

sentences.zh: 曆婺源尉、蘄廬建康三郡教授，改秩知溧陽縣。

translations.literal: He served as Wuyuan magistrate and professor of three prefectures—Qi, Lu, and Jiankang—and changed rank to govern Liyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate and professor, then governed Liyang County.

sentences.zh: 會叛卒周德據府城，殺官吏。

translations.literal: When rebel soldiers Zhou De held the prefectural city and killed officials,
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Zhou De seized the prefectural seat and killed officials,

sentences.zh: 邦乂立縣獄囚趙明于庭，欲誅之，因諭之曰：「爾悉裏中豪傑，誠能集爾徒爲邑人誅賊，不惟宥爾罪，當上功畀爵。」

translations.literal: Bangyi set the county prisoner Zhao Ming in the court, wishing to execute him, and admonished: "You know all the local stalwarts of the village—if you truly can gather your band to kill the bandits for the county people, not only will your crime be pardoned, you will be reported for merit and enfeoffed."
translations.idiomatic: Bangyi brought prisoner Zhao Ming before the court, offering pardon and reward if he rallied local men to kill the rebels.

sentences.zh: 明即請行，邦乂飲之卮酒，使自去。

translations.literal: Ming immediately asked to go; Bangyi gave him a cup of wine and let him leave himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ming agreed; Bangyi gave him wine and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 越翼日，討平之。

translations.literal: The next day it was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels were crushed.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，金人至江上。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan the Jin reached the river.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan's third year the Jin reached the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 高宗如浙西，留右僕射杜充爲御營使，駐紮建康，命劉光世、韓世忠、王𤫉諸將悉聽充節制。

translations.literal: Gaozong went to western Zhe; Right Vice Director Du Chong was left as commissioner of the imperial camp, stationed at Jiankang; Liu Guangshi, Han Shizhong, Wang Yuan and other generals all heeded Chong's command.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong fled west; Du Chong held Jiankang with Liu Guangshi, Han Shizhong, and Wang Yuan under him.

sentences.zh: 充性酷而無謀，士心不附。

translations.literal: Chong's nature was harsh and without stratagem; soldiers' hearts did not attach.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong was cruel and inept; the army did not trust him.

sentences.zh: 渡碙沙，充遣陳淬、岳飛等及金人戰于馬家渡。

translations.literal: Crossing Qisha, Chong sent Chen Cui, Yue Fei, and others to battle the Jin at Majia Ford.
translations.idiomatic: At Qisha he sent Chen Cui and Yue Fei to fight at Majia Ford.

sentences.zh: 自辰至未，戰數合，勝負未決。

translations.literal: From chen to wei they fought several bouts; victory and defeat were not decided.
translations.idiomatic: From morning to afternoon they fought without clear victory.

sentences.zh: 𤫉擁兵弗救，淬被擒，𤫉兵遁，充率麾下數千人降。

translations.literal: Wang Yuan held troops and did not rescue; Cui was captured; Yuan's troops fled; Chong led several thousand under him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan refused to help; Chen Cui was captured; Yuan fled; Du Chong surrendered with thousands.

sentences.zh: 金人濟江，鼓行逼城。

translations.literal: The Jin crossed the river and marched pressing the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin crossed and marched on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 時李棁以戶部尚書董軍餉，陳邦光以顯謨閣直學士守建康，皆具降狀，逆之十里亭。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zhi was Household Minister directing army provisions; Chen Bangguang as Direct Huixian Attendant guarded Jiankang—both prepared surrender documents and went ten li to the pavilion to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi and Chen Bangguang prepared surrender papers and met the Jin ten li out.

sentences.zh: 金帥完顏宗弼既入城，棁、邦光率官屬迎拜，惟邦乂不屈膝，以血大書衣裾曰：「甯作趙氏鬼，不爲他邦臣。」

translations.literal: Jin commander Wanyan Zongbi having entered the city, Zhi and Bangguang led officials to bow in welcome; only Bangyi would not bend the knee and in blood wrote large on his skirt: "Better be a ghost of the Zhao house than a minister of another state."
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi entered, officials bowed; Bangyi refused and wrote in blood on his robe: "Better be Zhao's ghost than another state's minister."

sentences.zh: 宗弼不能屈。

translations.literal: Zongbi could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi could not break him.

sentences.zh: 翼曰，遣人說邦乂，許以舊官。

translations.literal: The next day men were sent to persuade Bangyi, promising his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Next day they offered his old office.

sentences.zh: 邦乂以首觸柱礎流血，曰：「世豈有不畏死而可以利動者？

translations.literal: Bangyi struck his head on the pillar base until blood flowed, saying: "In the world is there one who does not fear death yet can be moved by profit?
translations.idiomatic: He smashed his head on a pillar until blood ran: "Is there anyone who does not fear death yet can be bought?

sentences.zh: 速殺我。」

translations.literal: Quickly kill me."
translations.idiomatic: Kill me at once."

sentences.zh: 翼日，宗弼等與棁、邦光宴堂上，立邦乂于庭，邦乂叱棁、邦光曰：「天子以若捍城，敵至不能抗，更與共宴樂，尚有面目見我乎？」

translations.literal: The next day Zongbi and others feasted with Zhi and Bangguang in the hall, standing Bangyi in the court; Bangyi reviled Zhi and Bangguang: "The Son of Heaven made you defend the city; when the enemy came you could not resist, yet you feast and rejoice with them—do you still have face to see me?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day at Zongbi's feast he cursed the defectors in the hall.

sentences.zh: 有劉團練者，以幅紙書「死活」二字示邦乂曰：「若無多雲，欲死趣書'死'字。」

translations.literal: The next day Zongbi and others feasted with Zhi and Bangguang in the hall, standing Bangyi in the court; Bangyi reviled Zhi and Bangguang: "The Son of Heaven made you defend the city; when the enemy came you could not resist, yet you feast and rejoice with them—do you still have face to see me?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day at Zongbi's feast he cursed the defectors in the hall.

sentences.zh: 邦乂奮筆書「死」字，金人相顧動色，然未敢害也。

translations.literal: A Regimental Trainer Liu showed Bangyi a strip with the characters 'life' and 'death': "If you have nothing more to say, if you wish death hurry and write the character 'death'."
translations.idiomatic: Officer Liu offered paper marked life and death: "If you mean to die, write 'death.'"

sentences.zh: 已而宗弼再引邦乂，邦乂不勝憤，遙望大罵曰：「若女真圖中原，天寧久假汝，行磔汝萬段，安得汙我！」

translations.literal: Bangyi fiercely wrote the character 'death'; the Jin looked at each other and changed color, yet did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "death" boldly; the Jin exchanged glances but still did not kill him.

sentences.zh: 宗弼大怒，殺之，剖取其心，年四十四。

translations.literal: Later Zongbi again summoned Bangyi; Bangyi could not contain rage and from afar cursed loudly: "If you Jurchen covet the central plain, Heaven will not long lend you power—I will dismember you in ten thousand pieces—how could you defile me!"
translations.idiomatic: Summoned again, he cursed: "Heaven will not long favor you Jurchen—you will be torn apart—do not defile me!"

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈直秘閣，賜田三頃，官爲斂葬，即其地賜廟褒忠，諡忠襄，官其四子。

translations.literal: Zongbi was greatly angered and killed him, cut out his heart; he was forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi in fury killed him and cut out his heart; he was forty-four.

sentences.zh: 邦乂少處郡學，目不視非禮，同舍欲隳其守，拉之出，托言故舊家，實娼館也。

translations.literal: When the matter was heard, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Direct Secretariat Attendant, given three qing of fields, officials buried him, and at that place granted a temple Bao Zhong; posthumous title Zhongxiang; his four sons were given office.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously honored him, granted fields and a temple, named him Loyal and Steadfast, and ennobled his four sons.

sentences.zh: 邦乂初不疑，酒數行，娼女出，邦乂愕然，疾趨還舍，解其衣冠焚之，流涕自責。

translations.literal: In youth at the prefectural school Bangyi's eyes did not look at what was not ritual; schoolmates wishing to break his guard pulled him out, claiming an old friend's house—it was actually a brothel.
translations.idiomatic: As a student he avoided impropriety; classmates tricked him into a brothel.

sentences.zh: 紹興七年，樞密院言邦乂忠節顯著，上曰：「顏真卿異代忠臣，朕昨已官其子孫，邦乂爲朕死節，不可不厚褒錄，以爲忠義之勸。」

translations.literal: Bangyi at first did not suspect; after several rounds of wine the courtesan came out; Bangyi was startled, hurried back to his lodging, took off his hat and robes and burned them, and wept in self-reproach.
translations.idiomatic: He fled when the courtesan appeared, burned his clothes, and wept in shame.

sentences.zh: 加贈徽猷閣待制，增賜田三頃。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shaoxing the Bureau of Military Affairs said Bangyi's loyal integrity was outstanding; the emperor said: "Yan Zhenqing was a loyal minister of another age—I have already given office to his descendants; Bangyi died for me—he must be richly honored to encourage loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing's seventh year the Bureau of Military Affairs praised Bangyi; the emperor said Yan Zhenqing's line had been honored and Bangyi's martyrdom must be richly rewarded to encourage loyalty.
